title: Lenny's Growth Assistant
transcription: This assistant answers questions from 300 podcast episodes. Watch what happens when I ask it something those episodes don't cover. It refuses. That refusal is the hardest thing in this project, and it isn't a prompt instruction, it's enforced in code. Lenny's Podcast is hundreds of interviews with product and growth leaders. The insight you need is in there, but it is scattered. A question like, "How do I know I have product market fit?" gets answered by a dozen guests who disagree with each other. Search gives you fragments. A general chatbot gives you a fluent answer with invented attribution. I wanted both synthesis and sources. Still on the local model, it retrieves from Postgres using hybrid search, vector similarity fused with full-text ranking, and then answers only from what came back. Every claim carries a bracket, and every bracket resolves to a real episode and a named guest. If it can't cite it, it doesn't say it. A cloud model will follow an instruction like "only use these excerpts." A 1-billion-parameter local model won't. Asked that cooking question, it answered from its own memory and attached a citation to an unrelated excerpt so the answer looked sourced. So, scope became code. These rules only ever see the retrieval evidence, never your question, which means they can't quietly turn into a banned topic list. Three cheaper approaches failed first. I even asked the model to judge its own grounding. Two out of six, and in one case, it answered, "Yes, this is answerable," while its own reason said the excerpt didn't discuss the topic. There are four skills, and a three-tier router decides which one runs. Cheap pattern matching goes first. "Build me a dashboard" never needs a model call at all. Only genuinely ambiguous requests reach the LLM classifier, and that classifier also rewrites the search query because a conversational question makes a poor embedding. You can watch it decide in the logs: the skill, the tier, the confidence, and then the retrieval fan-out underneath. The second skill writes "Ship 30 for 30" essays: strong hook, short paragraphs, bolded phrases so it can be skimmed, a clear takeaway at the end, and citations running through it. This one measured at 1,301 words against a 1,250-word target, nine bold phrases, 10 bullets, five sources. The third skill generates artifacts. Asked for a dashboard, and it writes a complete HTML document that renders right here, sandboxed in an iframe. It never leaves the application. On the local model, the layout is deterministic. The design system comes from the app, and things like an empty table or a mismatched column count get repaired in code. So, a small model can produce a thin page, but not a broken one. The local model has real limits, and they are written down, including a claim in my own README that turned out to be wrong once I retested it. FastAPI, React, Postgres with pgvector, Claude, and Ollama behind a single interface. 182 tests. Thank you for watching.

transcription: In a collective quest to transform agri-food systems equitably and sustainably, we face a daunting challenge: analyzing the contributions of millions of scientists to inform future decisions. By aligning research with policy objectives, we guide inclusive and equitable decisions across food systems, and find solutions from scientists in hunger and climate crisis-affected countries. Together, we can use science to find solutions to transform agri-food systems. Join us in this important journey.

title: 30th Anniversary of Ecohydrology at UNESCO and 20 years of UNESCO Ecohydrology Demonstration Sites
transcription: This year marks a significant moment for the UNESCO IHP as we celebrate the 30th birthday of ecohydrology at UNESCO and 20 years of UNESCO ecohydrology demonstration sites. Today, we reflect back from foundations of the science in Poland to the current global influence of ecohydrology. Ecohydrology rose to answer the fundamental question of how to deal with ecosystem problems in the aquatic environment. As Professor Zalewski, director of the European Regional Centre for Ecohydrology, realized that environmental protection alone is not enough. Hence, by studying the mechanisms that regulate the environmental processes through the interactions between the biota and the water system, ecohydrology was born. With water as a driver for all life, the protection and resilience against challenges in the current climatic context, such as pollution, scarcity, management, and drought, is essential. Thus, the second part of ecohydrology is finding and implementing solutions. From the design of experiments in laboratories to the implementation of real systems, research in ecohydrology looks for nature-based solutions to tackle different problems worldwide. To highlight successful implementations of NBS based on ecohydrological values at the water basin scale, UNESCO has supported the formation of 66 demonstration sites. These span 36 countries across all six continents and are excellent case studies for the ecohydrological approach to water management. This network has developed thanks to the UNESCO demonstration site program that brings together researchers, local governments, and communities from all across the world. Examples include the ecological engineering of Las Dunas in the Cahuayumac microbasin in Peru, the natural migration and remediation of watersheds and lagoon ecosystem in Ghar El Melh, Tunisia, wastewater treatment wetland system in Asmelabad, Pakistan, and the Birmingham urban ecohydrological urban observatory in the Upper Tame catchment in the United Kingdom. Another key development is the international Ecohydrology & Hydrobiology Journal aimed at increasing understanding of water-biota interplay and how this knowledge can be used for decision-making tools. The scope aims to address the priorities of the international initiatives, such as the Millennium Development Goals and the UNESCO IHP. With 26 volumes, the journal incorporates climate change, water quality, pollution, and sustainability, and the latest developments of ecohydrological understanding. The importance of ecohydrology will continue to grow with the need to reduce consumption and alleviate pressure on the environment as climate change will bring about new water challenges. With water being a key element of all aspects of life, these 30 years mark only the beginning. To continue building a resilient future, we look to the youth of today. The Ecohydrology Youth Network brings together young people and aims to support the engagement and the development of ideas within the ecohydrology field. With over 500 members, the network connects young scientists, promotes ecohydrological solutions, and exchanges ideas. The future of ecohydrology is looking bluer and greener. And on that note, happy 30th anniversary of ecohydrology and 20 years of ecohydrology demonstration sites.

title: Antibiotics Exposure Within 6 Months is not Associated with Increased Prevalence of SIBO
transcription: Hi, my name is Dr. Gillian Barlow, and I'm here to talk about my poster about antibiotic resistance and the small bowel. Prolonged or repeated use of antibiotics, particularly in early childhood, can negatively impact the gut microbiome and lead to antibiotic resistance. In addition, antibiotic use has been suggested to contribute to the development of small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, or SIBO. However, most of these studies were performed using stool samples. So in this study, we explored the impact of antibiotic use in the small bowel, which is central to nutrient absorption, immune function, and hormone regulation. To do this, we collected duodenal aspirates from subjects undergoing upper endoscopy via our REIMAGINE study and isolated the microbial DNAs and sequenced them. We also plated some of each sample to determine which ones had SIBO, and compared medical histories to see which subjects had used antibiotics in the last six months. In total, 1,052 subjects were analyzed, of whom 214 had taken antibiotics in the last six months. Importantly, we found there was no significant difference in the prevalence of SIBO in subjects who had or had not taken antibiotics. In addition, there were also no differences in duodenal microbiome diversity or richness between the two groups. However, we did find significant differences in antibiotic resistance profiles. Comparing antibiotic resistance ontology, or ARO phenotypes, we found that two were more common in subjects who had taken antibiotics in the last six months. The first was proteins modulating permeability to antibiotics, which confers resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics, that would include penicillins, cephalosporins, and carbapenems. And the second was genes altering cell wall change, which confers resistance to a broad range of antibiotics. Lastly, as far more of the subjects in our antibiotics group were female, we broke the results down by sex. However, we found that there were no differences in the ARO profiles in male versus female subjects. So, what are our take-home messages? Taking antibiotics in the last six months is not associated with an increased prevalence of SIBO, and does not appear to affect microbiome richness or diversity in the small bowel. However, subjects who had taken antibiotics in the last six months did have increased prevalence of antibiotic resistance phenotypes that confer resistance to a broad range of antibiotics, and specifically to beta-lactam antibiotics. These differences were not significantly different between male and female subjects. Thank you for listening to my poster. Please check out all of the other research that the Mast Group is presenting at DDW 2023.

We're one of the largest groupings of neuroscientists in Europe, and home to a broad church of scientists looking at every aspect of the brain and how it develops and functions from the beginning to the very end of life. Uh people have looked at the sequencing, uh genomics of SIBO, um but nobody's really explored the proteomics of SIBO. So we're going to look at the protein makeup of people with or without SIBO, and see what sort of diagnostic or prognostic markers there are there. So, of the proteins we see, we see many IgGs, uh which is something we might expect to see in SIBO, and we also see Defensin A1 and Defensin A3 are one of the most significantly upregulated proteins in SIBO. So, if we look at the particular pathways that are in this dataset, we have many proteins that are part of the neutrophil degranulation pathway. And this highlights that there is a specific neutrophil response occurring to SIBO in the lumen. So, to summarize some of the important results we see, uh we see immunoglobulins and defensins in our protein dataset, which is something that we would expect to see in response to bacterial overgrowth. title: The Absolute Quantification of Gram-Negative Bacteria in Older Subjects with SIBO and GI Symptoms
transcription: Hi. My name is Ava from the MAST program. And in this study, we're looking at how aging impacts the small intestinal microbiome and its relationship to gastrointestinal symptoms. We know that small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, or SIBO, becomes more common as people get older. But what we're still unclear about is why. Whether it's driven by an increase in total bacterial load or shifts in the microbial composition, or even both. So our aim in this study is to determine if there's a relationship between aging, absolute small bowel microbial loads, microbial community structure, and gastrointestinal symptom severity. To address this, we analyzed duodenal aspirate samples from subjects in the REIMAGINE study. These were patients undergoing upper endoscopy without colon prep. We grouped subjects by age and used metagenomic sequencing to quantify absolute microbial abundance, so not just relative composition, but actual bacterial load. What we found is total bacterial load increases significantly with age, and the prevalence of SIBO rises as well. At the same time, microbial diversity declines in older age groups. When we looked more closely at microbial composition, we found that key Gram-negative bacteria, particularly Escherichia coli and Klebsiella species, increase progressively with age in patients with SIBO. These changes were consistent and significant across all age groups. Then we looked at how this relates to symptoms. In subjects over the age of 50, those with SIBO reported significantly greater symptom severity, including diarrhea, bloating, and abdominal pain. Importantly, these symptoms were strongly associated with the abundance of specific bacterial groups, such as Escherichia and Fusobacterium, rather than bacterial load alone. And also, in older subjects without SIBO, increased bacterial load did not correlate with symptom severity. So simply having more bacteria isn't enough to explain symptoms. It really depends on the microbial composition. So overall, our findings suggest that aging is associated with increased bacterial load and reduced diversity, but symptom severity in older adults is more closely linked to specific microbial signatures rather than total load alone. This highlights the importance of using absolute microbial quantification to better understand, diagnose, and potentially treat SIBO, especially in aging populations. Thank you so much for taking the time to listen to my poster, and be sure to check out the rest of our posters from the MAST program here at DDW. Take care.

title: Journal with Me: Master Your Mindset (in 2026)
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: There is this poem that says our soul is the sail of our life and how our soul is set determines how our life goes. Have you believed the lie that the winds matter more than your sail? The winds around us are ferocious forces, that is for sure. But they are not what guides us. Darling, the winds change with seasons, with tempests, and those who forget their sail are surely at the wind's mercy, tossed and directionless. Raise your sail, dear one. With it, you will use the winds to set the direction, the course of your life. Happiness, bliss, shalom, peace exists in one place—inside of you—and in one time—right now. This ancient wisdom is your sail. You are the gatekeeper, the manager of your sacred space. Therefore, commune daily with her. Ask, "How is she?" For as she goes, so does the rest of life. And when we get tempted to wrench that soul into conforming, into behaving, into lockstep with every other soul, we must remember that she is a wild spirit, that her dreams are not meant for others' validation, that she sways the oaks and sends cracks through Earth's tectonic plates when she realizes the power and beauty of her sail. These two things can be true at the same time: treacherous winds are blowing and your soul is set on peace, hope, love, and joy.

title: "What It Sounds Like" Huntrix | Live Action Music Video | KPop Demon Hunters | Song Cover | IRL Sony
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription:
Nothing but the truth now.
Nothing but the proof
of what I am.
The worst of what I came from.
Patterns I'm ashamed of.
Things that even I don't understand.
I tried to fix it. I tried to fight it.
My head was twisted.
My heart divided.
My lives all collided.
I don't know why I
didn't trust you
to be on my side.
I broke into a million pieces
and I can't go back.
But now I'm seeing all the beauty
in the broken glass.
These scars are part of me,
darkness and harmony.
My voice will be the light.
This is what it sounds like.
Why did I cover up
the colors stuck inside my head?
I should have let the jagged edges
meet the light instead.
Show me what's underneath.
I'll find your harmony.
The song we couldn't write.
This is what it sounds like.
Stop this song.
We're shattering the silent.
We're rising, defiant,
shining in the quiet.
You're not alone.
We listen to the demons.
We let them get between us.
But none of us are out here
on our own.
So we were cowards,
so we were liars,
so we're no heroes,
we're still survivors.
The dreamers, the fighters.
No lying, I'm tired.
But dive in the fire
and I'll be right here
by your side.
We broke into a million pieces
and we can't go back.
But now we're seeing all the beauty
in the broken glass.
These scars are part of me,
darkness and harmony.
My voice will be the light.
This is what it sounds like.
Why did we cover up
the colors stuck inside our head?
Get up and let the jagged edges
meet the light instead.
Show me what's underneath.
I'll find your harmony.
Fearless and on the fire.
This is what it sounds like.
G-Crew.

title: Journal Reading 010 | Trust Your Journey, It Was Carved For You
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: There was a point in time, earlier on in my spiritual awakening journey, when I was concerned with growth and getting better. Not that I don't want to grow now because of course I do, but in the beginning, the pursuit of growth was all-consuming. It was ego-driven. I went to the gym regularly, I meditated, I read self-help, spiritual books, and took notes. I even took up coaching others in an attempt to ditch the nine-to-five scene. None of the habits stuck for more than a few months, but I would always come back to them the following year. Like I said, it was ego-driven. I wanted to do better because, deep down, I felt I wasn't good enough. I felt behind in life, like I should be further along. And although that way of pursuing growth and self-improvement served its purpose, I now understand it's not the best way. Actually, I would even go as far as to say as adding habits to your daily routine for the sole purpose of getting better is the very thing that keeps you from getting better. Often times, our pursuit for better is rooted in social validation. We want to be liked, we want to be accepted, we want to be seen in a particular light. And the problem doesn't come from not being noticed or liked. Often times, along these sorts of external focus journeys, we are seen and liked, but we aren't seen and liked for who we actually are. I believe a better way to improve oneself is not to download a bunch of habits influencers have said that have changed their lives, but to do more of the things you enjoy. Lean into yourself, and forget what the internet says is good or bad. If running is what you love, then run because you love it, not because you think in three months you'll be a different person. If you genuine- if you genuinely enjoy having a couple of beers at the end of the day, have a couple of beers. The biggest lie the self-improvement space sold us was that there's something wrong with who we are, and that we need to fix it. There is nothing wrong with who you are or where you are at in life. We are all walking our own paths, evolving at our own pace. Don't let a stranger on the internet make you feel less than you are. True and lasting change will come when you're ready. And when you're ready, the change will be effortless. Trust your journey. It was carved for you. Thank you for watching. Have a good day.

title: Finding True Abundance | Journal Reading 019
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Good morning, YouTube. Today's journal reading was written on March 17th, 2026, and in this one, I kind of explore ideas of abundance, and I think that's a theme that maybe I've wrestled with a lot throughout my life. Anyway, here it goes. Abundance is found in nothing. Abundance is found in knowing enough. As I write this, I'm sitting back in our brown leather recliner we found sitting outside our dumpster when we first moved here. That probably sounds gross, but it was in good shape, and we needed some furniture. That was roughly six years ago. There was a time in my life where material abundance and worldly status mattered to me. It was something I chased. Where I was, or what I had, was never enough. I needed more. I needed to progress. But then something changed. I don't know when it happened, or why, or what triggered it. All I know is one day, all that once mattered seemed trivial. Among the spiritual community, there's a decent amount of talk about abundance, the law of attraction, and manifestation. If only we align our thoughts and energy with the life and success and the material we desire, all we imagine will be ours. Whether there's any truth to that, that doesn't really matter to me. What does matter to me is why our lives, where we are at this—where—lah, where we are at any given moment is not enough for us. I think we all have ideas in our head of what it means to be abundant and successful, and likely more often than not, those ideas are filled with lavish material items and social recognition from our fellow man. It's what I thought. It's what I chased. But I've come to understand that that's not true abundance. That's not what true success is. True success and abundance is looking around at your life just at it—just as it is right now, and seeing all that you have, all that you've accomplished this far. If you live in America, odds are you have everything you need, plus some. You have a roof over your head, food in the fridge, people who love you. Recognizing the value in all of that you already have is true abundance. Knowing enough in a world that is constantly telling you to go for more, to go for better, is a superpower. It's abundance. Knowing enough is not a lack mindset. It's peaceful sustainability. It's the mindset of the richest people on earth.

title: Fix Your Messy Life | The Bullet Journal Method | Ryder Carroll | chapter 4 (B01_0001_04)
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Bullet journaling accepts that every day is different rather than trying to impose the same structure each time. This makes it flexible and able to handle whatever comes up. The main point is that bullet journaling embraces chaos with a system that can change as needed. A daily log has not set amount of space, use what you need that day. Some days may take just one page, others more. The monthly log has two pages, one for the calendar and one for tasks. Write events, tasks and notes on the calendar page next to each date. List tasks for the month on the other page. If a task is for a different month, write it in the future log, then add future tasks to the next month's log when that month starts. You can make custom pages for specific topics like health goals or a hobby. Use the index at the front to keep track of all your pages and collections. List the topic and page numbers. Keep adding to the index as needed. This flexible approach accepts that every day is different. The system can grow and change along with your need.

title: 5-4-3-2-1 Secret Method | The Bullet Journal Method | Ryder Carroll | chapter 6 (B01_0001_06)
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Your bullet journal can be a useful tool for setting and achieving meaningful goals. Start by making a goals collection to write down both big and small goals. This helps transform vague dreams into real objectives. Next, create timelines for your goals, using something like the 5-4-3-2-1 method. Identify goals for the next 5 years, 4 months, 3 weeks, 2 days and 1 hour. You will likely have many goals, so prioritize by carefully considering each one. Ask yourself if the goal is really important and worth the effort. Choose one personal and one professional goal in each timeframe, for a total of 10 priority goals. It's important to regularly re-evaluate your goals to make sure they still matter. One way is with goal sprints, breaking big goals into smaller steps to test your commitment. This can help you focus on goals that inspire you and keep you motivated, long term. Clarification and prioritizing will help make your goals a reality.

title: Just do the right thing. The rest doesn’t matter.#Selflessness#PersonalGrowth#selfimprovement
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: On action and duty. Great ideas from the book Meditations by Marcus Aurelius. Just do the right thing, the rest doesn't matter. That quote is basically saying focus on what you can control, and let go of what you can't. Here's what that breaks down to. 1. Just do the right thing. This is the part you can control. It's about your own choices, your own actions, and your own character. Is it kind? Is it honest? Is it helpful? Does it align with who you want to be? Your job is to figure out the right, decent, ethical thing to do in a situation and then do it. That's your duty. 2. The rest doesn't matter. This is the part you can't control, so don't let it paralyze you or stop you from doing your duty. What other people think of you for doing it, whether you'll get credit or even be thanked, whether it will be successful or work out perfectly, how hard or scary it feels. The outcome, sometimes, you can only control your effort, not the final result. Think of it like this. You see someone drop their wallet. The right thing is to pick it up and give it back to them. So you do it. The rest, that doesn't matter. Whether they are suspicious of you, whether they say a heartfelt thank you or just grunt, or whether you're late to your next appointment because you stopped. You did your part. The rest was out of your hands. In a nutshell, pour your energy into being a person of good action. Don't waste your energy worrying about the noise, the results, or the opinions that follow. Your peace comes from knowing you did what you should, not from how the world reacts. It's a call for integrity over image, for courage over comfort, and for focusing on your own behavior in a world you can't control.

title: How to Build Habits That Actually Stick
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: You're not failing when it comes to habits. You're just starting too many at once. Most people don't struggle because they're lazy. They struggle because they try to change their entire life overnight. They want to wake up earlier, start working out, eat healthier, drink more water, meditate, journal, read more, spend less time on their phone, all at the same time. And for a few days, it feels exciting, but then everything falls apart. Not because you're incapable, because your brain can't sustain that much change all at once. If your habits never seem to stick, the problem isn't motivation. It's the way you're trying to build them. Most habits fail because there's no structure behind them. People rely on motivation instead of systems. They tell themselves, "I'll work out after work tomorrow. I'll start eating healthier in a few days. I'll remember to do it." But vague habits don't survive real life because life gets busy, you get tired, your routine changes, your motivation drops, and if there's no repeatable structure, the habit disappears with it. Another mistake people make is setting the barrier too high. They think, "If I'm going to work out, I'm going to do 1 hour. If I'm going to read, I need to read an entire chapter. If I'm going to meal prep, I need to fix my entire diet." Eventually, your brain starts resisting it, not because the goal is bad, because the effort required feels too big to repeat consistently. That's why intensity usually fails. It asks too much before consistency exists. If you want a habit to stick, make it smaller, smaller than you think it should be. Make it so easy your brain has no reason to avoid it. Want to start working out? Don't commit to an hour. Commit to putting your shoes on and doing 5 to 10 minutes. Want to read more? Read one page. Want to meditate? Sit down for 30 seconds. Your goal in the beginning should not be full transformation. It should be repetition because repetition creates familiarity and familiarity lowers resistance. You're not trying to prove how disciplined you are. You should be trying to teach your brain that this is something you do now. Another thing that helps is attaching your habits to something that already exists. Instead of saying, "I'll do it later," anchor it to something specific. After I brush my teeth, I'll stretch. After work, I'll take a walk for 10 minutes. After making my coffee, I'll journal for a few minutes. The less decisions your brain has to make, the easier consistency becomes. That's what systems do. They reduce friction. Here's the part that nobody likes hearing. Consistency is supposed to feel boring sometimes. Social media makes change look exciting and intense, but real progress usually looks repetitive, quiet, simple, unimpressive. A lot of people quit because a habit no longer feels exciting. But habits that last aren't built on excitement. They're built on repeatability. You don't need perfect days. You need enough days repeated over time. Missing one day isn't failure. Starting over every single week is. The goal isn't to become a different person overnight. The goal is to create a system that you can maintain over time. If you want habits that actually stick, stop trying to change everything at once. Make the habit smaller. Remove friction. Repeat it consistently. Build structure around it. Because consistency is not built through intensity. It's built through repetition. Small actions repeated daily will always beat out massive effort that only lasts a week. Until one day, they become automatic. If this helped, subscribe. I'll be breaking down systems for your lifestyle so you can actually build something that works.

title: UKREiiF 2026: 'Where the smart money is moving' panel discussion
transcription: So, we're here at UKREIIF this year, talking all things living UK real estate. The current environment for living real estate in the UK is one with viability challenges and concerns. We've got rising build cost inflation, increased regulation, economic difficulties. What there also is, is a huge amount of opportunity. There is pent-up demand, there is under supply, there is no shortage of debt available, there is capital being deployed. It is a huge time for opportunity. The smart money is moving primarily into affordable housing, I would say, though how you define that depends on a number of factors, but clearly the biggest risk to any investment strategy is take-up and demand at this moment, and so through various lenses people are trying to make sure that whatever it is that they're investing in or developing is affordable for the end user, so that the project is viable long-term. I think there's quite a lot of opportunity for living product, because there is a fundamental requirement and demand for good quality accommodation across all the living sectors, asset classes. Especially when there is a bit of an affordability gap. So, those that can deliver product that meets that demand are going to be very well placed. 2026, for me, has also been the year of co-living. We're seeing more institutionalisation of co-living, in terms of an accepted asset class for co-investors. So, I think the opportunities at the moment, very much from a housebuilders point of view, are in the land market. Slightly longer-term strategic sites, gray belt, something where you can work with a landowner to really maximize the number of homes on a site, and really go out there and get a planning consent. I believe that the opportunities in the living sector lie in working in partnership, both with local governments, local councils, with developers, with capital, trying to bring everybody together to achieve the ultimate goal of delivering more housing for the country. I think the smart money in living is moving to affordable with a small 'a'. That's how we deal with the viability concerns. That's where some degree of public subsidy can unlock delivery. I also see there's huge opportunities in partnerships becoming platforms, with long-term sustainable partnerships between registered providers, developers and investors to unlock delivery at scale.

transcription: आशीष, आपसे शुरुआत करते हैं। इंडेक्स स्टॉक पहले BEL। क्या एक्सपेक्ट करें? स्टेडी नंबर्स यहां पर देखने को मिल सकते हैं। अच्छा BEL में ख़ास बात ये होती है कि मैं ब्रोकरेज हाउस की रिपोर्ट्स पढ़ रहा था कि क्वार्टरली बेसिस पर हर बार क्योंकि प्रोडक्ट मिक्स अलग-अलग होता है तो हर बार मार्जिन एक जैसे या फिर हर बार मार्जिन में ग्रोथ आप एक्सपेक्ट करके नहीं चल सकते। ख़ास बात होती है कि आर्डर बुक कैसी है, एग्जीक्यूशन कैसा देखने को मिला और टॉपलाइन कैसी है। ये BEL के केस में बड़ा इंपॉर्टेंट होता है। तो सबसे पहले आप देखें तो टॉपलाइन काफी हेल्दी है, कारण ये कि आर्डर इनफ्लो बहुत अच्छा रहा है। पूरे FY24 में देखें या क्वार्टर 4 में, तक़रीबन 14% की बढ़त यहां पर एक्सपेक्टेड है। 10,371 करोड़ का अनुमान मार्केट लगाकर चल रहा है। अगर आप आपरेशनल फ्रंट पर देखें तो स्टेडी क्वार्टर है, हालांकि कोई गिरावट नहीं है, बढ़त भी नहीं है, 2% के आसपास के चेंज आपको देखने को मिलेंगे। और मार्जिन जैसा कि मैंने बताया कि प्रोडक्ट मिक्स के ऊपर बहुत ज्यादा डिपेंड करता है तो जो 30.6% का एबिटा मार्जिन पिछले साल थे, अब इस बार 27.4 देखने को मिल सकते हैं और मुनाफे का आंकड़ा भी बिल्कुल फ्लैट है, कोई बढ़त नहीं है, सिर्फ 3% की ग्रोथ यहां पर देखने को मिलेगी। लेकिन बड़ा इंपॉर्टेंट होता है कि एग्जीक्यूशन कैसा है। तो इस क्वार्टर के दौरान एग्जीक्यूशन क्योंकि वैसे भी इनकी तरफ से जो अपडेट आया था क्वार्टर 4 का, उसमें पता चल रहा था कि एग्जीक्यूशन बढ़िया देखने को मिला है और आर्डर इनफ्लो की बात करें तो 11,200 करोड़ के आसपास यानी पिछले साल के मुकाबले 30% ज्यादा है। एक्सपोर्ट की रेवेन्यू, एक्सपोर्ट के ऑर्डर्स ये लगातार बढ़ रहे हैं, पिछले साल के मुकाबले एक्सपोर्ट की रेवेन्यू 34% बढ़ सकती है और ख़ास तौर पर इनका एग्जीक्यूशन इनके की-प्रोडक्ट्स में कैसा है, इसका मार्केट पर ज्यादा फोकस रहेगा। नंबर्स के लिहाज से आप एटलीस्ट स्टेडी नंबर्स एक्सपेक्ट करके चल सकते हैं। स्टेडी नंबर्स फ्रॉम BEL। ये आशीष ने अगर आप देखें, एक्सपेक्टेशन जाहिर की, पूर्वानुमान में।

title: TCS Q4 Results 2026 : Tata की कंपनी ने रचा इतिहास, शेयर पर दिखेगा सीधा असर! | BIZ Tak
transcription: नमस्कार, आप देख रहे हैं बिस्तख और मैं हूं आपके साथ चिराग ठाकुर। देश की दिग्गज आईटी कंपनी टाटा कंसल्टेंसी सर्विसेज यानी कि टीसीएस ने गुरुवार को अपने चौथे तिमाही के नतीजे जारी किए, जिसमें कंपनी का प्रदर्शन मजबूत रहा। कंपनी का कंसोलिडेटेड नेट प्रॉफिट सालाना आधार पर 12% बढ़कर ₹13,718 करोड़ पहुंच गया। पिछले साल इसी तिमाही में यह ₹12,224 करोड़ था। कंपनी ने ₹31 प्रति शेयर का फाइनल डिविडेंड घोषित किया है। इससे निवेशकों को सीधा फायदा मिलेगा। टीसीएस का ऑपरेशन से रेवेन्यू 10% बढ़कर ₹70,698 करोड़ हो गया है। कंपनी को यह फायदा ऐसे समय में हुआ है जब आईटी सेक्टर आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस में नए-नए बदलाव के कारण उतार-चढ़ाव भरे दौर से गुजर रहा है। इस कारण कंपनी के शेयरों में हाल में बड़ी गिरावट आई थी। टीसीएस ने इस तिमाही में 12 अरब डॉलर की कुल डील वैल्यू यानी कि टीसीबी हासिल की है। जिसमें तीन बड़ी मेगा डील शामिल है। कंपनी की विकास दर में आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस की भूमिका सबसे अहम रही है। कंपनी की सीओओ आरती सुब्रमण्यम के अनुसार FY26 एआई अपनाने के मामले में एक निर्णायक साल रहा। चौथी तिमाही में कंपनी का सालाना एआई रेवेन्यू 2.3 अरब डॉलर के पार निकल गया है। टीसीएस ने अपने हाइपरवोल्ड निवेश के जरिए ओपनएआई, एएमडी और एबीबी जैसी दिग्गज कंपनियों के साथ रणनीतिक हाथ मिलाया है। कंपनी ने इंटरप्राइज ट्रांसफॉर्मेशन, डिजिटल इंजीनियरिंग और क्लाउड मॉर्डनाइजेशन जैसे क्षेत्रों में मजबूत डील्स हासिल किया है। कंपनी ने माना की वैश्विक आर्थिक चुनौतियां बनी हुई हैं लेकिन ग्राहकों का टेक्नोलॉजी निवेश पर भरोसा मजबूत है। नतीजों के ऐलान से पहले बीएसई पर टीसीएस का शेयर 1.09% की तेजी के साथ ₹2587.75 पर बंद हुआ। एक्सपर्ट का मानना है कि शानदार मार्जिन और एआई क्षेत्र में कंपनी की बढ़ती पकड़ आने वाले समय में स्टॉक को और मजबूती दे सकती है। इसके अलावा, टीसीएस ने 1 अप्रैल से सभी ग्रेड के कर्मचारियों के लिए सालाना सैलरी बढ़ोतरी लागू करने का ऐलान किया है। हालांकि, इस बार कितनी बढ़ोतरी होगी इसका खुलासा नहीं किया गया है। खास बात यह है कि कंपनी एक तरफ सैलरी बढ़ा रही है तो दूसरी तरफ कुल कर्मचारियों की संख्या में सालाना आधार पर कमी भी देखने को मिली है। हालांकि, इस बार सबसे बड़ा सवाल यही है कि सैलरी में कितनी बढ़ोतरी होगी। कंपनी ने अभी तक हाइक का परसेंट स्पष्ट नहीं किया है। पिछले साल FY25 में टीसीएस ने सैलरी हाइक में करीब 5 महीने की देरी की थी और सितंबर 2025 से इसे लागू किया गया था। उस समय औसतन 4.5% से 7% तक की बढ़ोतरी दी गई थी। जबकि बेहतर प्रदर्शन करने वाले कर्मचारियों को डबल डिजिट हाइक मिला था। आप टीसीएस के नतीजों के बारे में क्या सोचते हैं, कमेंट करके हमें जरूर बताएं और बने रहे बिस्तख के साथ।

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 explained: How the new 48-team format works
transcription: For years, FIFA President Gianni Infantino has talked about getting more countries involved at a World Cup. That push finally took shape in January 2017 when football's governing body voted to expand the tournament from 32 to 48 teams. Under the new format, there will be 104 matches at this World Cup. That's 40 more than at Qatar 2022. Those games will be played across 16 host cities in the USA, Mexico, and Canada. That's a huge change from the compact 2022 tournament in Qatar where a fan could realistically attend two or even three matches in a single day. The 48 teams will be split into 12 groups of four. The top two from each group plus the eight best third-placed teams will move into a new 32-team knockout phase. From there, the tournament runs through the round of 32, the round of 16, quarterfinals, semifinals, and then the final. By the time we get to the decider at MetLife Stadium in New York, New Jersey, on July the 19th, the champions will have played eight matches. That's one more than the seven required by Argentina when they won Qatar 2022.

का रेवेन्यू आपको फ्लैट ही देखने को मिल रहा है। कंपनी शो किया है 573 करोड़ का रेवेन्यू इस क्वार्टर में जबकि मार्केट को लग रहा था कि शायद इस क्वार्टर में कंपनी का बिज़नेस थोड़े से बेहतर आपको देखने को मिल title: The 2026 FIFA World Cup explained in 2 minutes
transcription: The stage is set for this year's FIFA Men's World Cup, with the opening matches kicking off tomorrow. The tournament, held every four years, will be unlike any before it. Here's why. Firstly, it will be the biggest World Cup in history, the most complex one yet. For the first time ever, the tournament will be shared across three countries: the United States, Canada, and Mexico, and matches will be played across 16 cities. The competition is expanding, too. Instead of the traditional eight groups, this year's tournament will feature 12, made up of four teams each. 48 national teams will compete, instead of 32. With more teams in the mix, the road to glory could be tougher to predict. The expansion means a record number of matches. Teams will play 104 matches over 39 days, making it the longest ever World Cup run. With more teams involved, there could be more opportunities for underdogs to make their mark. Among those returning to the World Cup include the Democratic Republic of Congo, Haiti, and Iraq, while four debutants are getting their boots on the pitch for the first time. They are Uzbekistan, Jordan, Curacao, and Cape Verde. But staging the World Cup across three countries brings major logistical challenges. Some teams could end up traveling thousands of kilometers between venues, crossing borders and time zones. FIFA has grouped matches regionally to reduce travel, but long journeys may still be unavoidable for teams that progress deep into the tournament. And depending on where they're playing, the climates could be different, from the high altitude of Mexico City to Miami's heat and humidity. To manage that, FIFA has mandated cooling and hydration breaks during matches. Next, technology will play a bigger role than ever before. Every player will have a digital avatar to remodel on-pitch actions. These changes make it easier for officials to see what would go on during fast or obstructed plays, so they can provide more accurate calls for offsides or potential handballs. And then, of course, there are the stars. This could be the last dance for several legends. Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo has confirmed this will be his last World Cup. Argentina's Lionel Messi and Croatia's Luka Modrić are also widely expected to be making their final appearances on the game's biggest stage. For football's greats, one final bow. For a new generation, a chance to make history. The road to World Cup glory is about to begin.

title: How Mohammad Irfan Went From Street Hawker To India's Most Viral Protest Voice
transcription: सिर्फ पेट रोटी खा लेना ही जीवन नहीं है। शहरी सलम में जीवन नरक है। मैं कहता हूँ लोकतंत्र में ना अहंकार नहीं संवाद होना चाहिए और संवाद के दरवाज़े दोनों तरफ़ से खुले होने चाहिए। संविधान की शपथ में ना गरिमा शब्द का, व्यक्ति की गरिमा, राष्ट्र की एकता और अखंडता को सुनिश्चित, तो व्यक्ति की गरिमा, गरिमा, गरिमा नहीं गिरनी चाहिए सर। जय श्री कृष्णा सर, मैं इरफ़ान सर और आज मुझे आपसे बहुत सारी बातें करनी है सर। चार ट्रिलियन की अर्थव्यवस्था में ना पढ़े-लिखों का ही जीवन संवरा है? A voice that rose about the slogans at Jantar Mantar is now being heard in the country's political corridors. Mohammad Irfan, the hawker with little formal education whose speeches went viral during the student protest, met Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Monday. Rahul Gandhi said Irfan's understanding of the constitution and his desire to learn reflected the strength of India's youth. Hours after the meet, Irfan spoke exclusively to India Today's sister platform, The Lallantop, with a message that cuts across party lines. मैं आज राहुल गांधी से मिला तो मैंने उनसे यही कहा कि अगर सर आप जो हम आपसे अपनी मांगे रख रहे हैं, आप विपक्ष के बड़े नेता हैं और आज नहीं तो कल सत्ता में आएंगे, अगर आपने हमारी बातों के वादाखिलाफी की तो हम अपनी असहमति आपके खिलाफ भी रखेंगे। For Irfan, accountability does not stop with one government or one political party. और हम न्यूट्रल हैं, हम इस देश का भला चाहते हैं। He also spoke about the struggles of migrant workers. 2024 का एनसीआरबी का डाटा कहता है कि 1 लाख 70 हजार 746 मौतें हुई जिसमें 31% दिहाड़ी मजदूर थे और वजह एक थी कि घर में तंगी और मानसिक संतुलन डिस्टर्ब होना, आर्थिक तंगी थी। तो हम कैसे इग्नोर कर सकते हैं उस वर्ग को जो इस देश की बड़ी आबादी है और खून-पसीना लगा रही है इस देश के निर्माण में? हम कैसे इग्नोर कर सकते हैं उसे? From the streets of Jantar Mantar to the national spotlight, his story is not about political power. It's about the power of a citizen's voice to be heard. Outside this Adams County courthouse, the sound of victory.

I didn't win. America won. America still has freedom of speech. It's still for the people, by the people.

This raid taking place nearly a year ago following search warrants related to possession and trafficking in drugs and kidnapping. The rapper was never charged. transcription: संजू सैमसन फॉर द फर्स्ट टाइम इन सीएसके कैंप आप ये सींस देख रहे हैं। यहां पे संजू सैमसन ने पैड्स वियर किए और थोड़ी बहुत नॉकिंग की। आप देख रहे हैं उनकी ये टिपिकल बैक एंड अक्रॉस मूवमेंट और उसके बाद फॉरवर्ड पुश। क्या खूबसूरत बल्लेबाज हैं। वर्ल्ड कप में अमेजिंग दिखाई दिए थे। ये आप एक और विजुअल्स के साथ देख सकते हैं कि नॉकिंग करते दिखाई दिए सिर्फ संजू सैमसन। नेट्स के अंदर बड़े शॉट लगाने की कोशिश नहीं की क्योंकि वो ज़्यादातर बिजी रहे हैं। एक प्रोमो को शूट कर रहे हैं। ये आप देख रहे हैं डिजिटल बाउंड्री के साथ वो यहां पे एक्सरसाइज कर रहे थे और उनके अलावा आप देख रहे हैं थला धोनी है जो कि रनिंग कर रहे हैं, प्रैक्टिस कर रहे हैं, बड़े-बड़े शॉट्स लगाने की कोशिश कर रहे हैं। हम आपको ये थला धोनी के डिफरेंट शॉट्स भी दिखा रहे हैं जिसमें उनका ये एक नो-लुक शॉट भी है। सो, थला धोनी बहुत अच्छी फॉर्म में नजर आ रहे हैं और अच्छे से रिदम में लग रहे हैं। सो, थला धोनी फिटनेस भी अपनी मेंटेन किए हुए हैं। संजू सैमसन आप देख सकते हैं कि यहां पे मौजूद थे और यहां पे पहले प्रैक्टिस सेशन जो था सीएसके का उसमें उन्होंने पार्टिसिपेट किया। ज़्यादातर बैटिंग तो नहीं की लेकिन वार्म-अप करते दिखाई दिए, नॉकिंग करते दिखाई दिए और थोड़ी बहुत उन्होंने एक्सरसाइज भी की। सो, ही हैज़ ऑफिशियली जॉइंड द कैंप। लेकिन ज़्यादातर उन्होंने टाइम फोटोशूट में गुजारा क्योंकि एक प्रोमो बन रहा है सीएसके का, आईपीएल के लिए और टीम के लिए। हम आपको ऐसी अपडेट्स देते रहेंगे। हमारे चैनल को सब्सक्राइब करके रखें। टिल नेक्स्ट अपडेट, गुड बाय।

title: CSK Roar 26 Match - CSK Roar Event 2026 | CSK Roar 26 Match Highlights
transcription: दोस्तों, IPL 2024 की स्टार्टिंग से पहले आज हम सभी लोगों को CSK की टीम का रोर इवेंट देखने को मिला था। जहाँ पर करंटली यह रोर इवेंट हमें चलता हुआ नज़र आ रहा है, इसमें हमें सबसे पहले तो चेन्नई सुपर किंग्स की टीम के जितना भी पुराना बैच था जिसमें मैथ्यू हेडन उनके साथ ही सुरेश रैना, अंबाती रायडू, हरभजन सिंह जैसे बड़े-बड़े प्लेयर्स फोटोशूट का हिस्सा बनते हुए नज़र आए थे। दरअसल, CSK की टीम जिन्होंने काफी सारे रिकॉर्ड ऑलरेडी बना दिए हैं, उन सभी प्लेयर्स को यहाँ पर सम्मानित किया गया था। इसके बाद, CSK के रोर मैच में हमें लाइव महेंद्र सिंह धोनी, संजू सैमसन और उसके साथ ही शिवम दुबे की काफी ज्यादा रॉयल एंट्री चेपॉक स्टेडियम में देखने को मिली। जिस तरीके से RCB का अनबॉक्स इवेंट होता है, कुछ उसी तर्ज पर काफी ज्यादा हाइप और क्रेज़ हमें देखने को मिला पूरी तरीके से जैम पैक्ड स्टेडियम। चेपॉक स्टेडियम में करंटली हमें देखने को मिल रहा है जहाँ पर MSD की एंट्री पर लोग काफी ज्यादा इमोशनल भी हो गए थे। इसके साथ ही, अभी हमें करंटली इसके बाद यहाँ पर एक मुकाबला भी देखने को मिलने वाला है जिसमें जो इनकी पास्ट की इलेवन है, जिसमें काफी बड़े-बड़े लेजेंड्स मैथ्यू हेडन, सुरेश रैना, रॉबिन उथप्पा, हरभजन सिंह जैसे प्लेयर्स पार्टिसिपेट करेंगे और जो करंट इलेवन है, उसमें महेंद्र सिंह धोनी और उनके साथ ही इनके करंट प्लेयर्स के बीच में हमें मुकाबला देखने को मिलने वाला है। तो CSK... आप लोग बताना क्या आप लोगों के हिसाब से इस साल CSK की टीम IPL का टाइटल जीतेगी या फिर नहीं?

title: MI Practice Match Highlight 2026 | MI Intra Squad Practice Match 2026 | Rohit Batting MI Camp 2026
transcription: दोस्तों IPL 2026 के एडिशन के लिए फाइनली मुंबई इंडियंस का भी प्रैक्टिस कैंप यहां पर शुरू हो चुका है जहां पर मुंबई की टीम ने भी आज इंट्रा स्क्वाड प्रैक्टिस मुकाबला खेला था। अपनी स्क्रीन पर देख पा रहे होंगे जहां पर रोहित 11 और शार्दुल ठाकुर 11 बनाकर यहां पर प्रैक्टिस मुकाबला खेला था। शार्दुल 11 ने टॉस जीतकर पहले बल्लेबाजी का फैसला किया था। शार्दुल 11 की तरफ से रोबिन मिंज़ इसके साथ ही राज अंगद बावा यहां पर बैटिंग करने आए थे। रोबिन मिंज़ ने यहां पर 32 गेंदों में 66 रन की ताबड़तोड़ पारी खेली थी। राज अंगद ने यहां पर 30 रन केवल 14 गेंदों में बनाए थे बेहतरीन शुरुआत दी थी। इसके साथ ही मयंक रावत ने 45 रन 29 गेंदों में बनाए थे और गेंद के साथ 34 रन देकर एक विकेट भी लिया था। इसके साथ ही शार्दुल ठाकुर ने फिनिशिंग टचेस दी थी, 10 गेंदों में 23 रन बनाए थे, दो विकेट लेकर 45 रन देकर दो विकेट भी इन्होंने लिए थे। मयंक मार्कंडेय ने 30 रन देकर एक विकेट लिया था। दीपक चाहर ने यहां पर 34 रन देकर एक विकेट लिया था। इसके साथ ही यहां पर 198 रन 9 विकेट पर 20 ओवर में यहां पर शार्दुल 11 ने बनाए थे। दरअसल बॉल बाय बॉल इसके साथ ही जो फास्ट हाईलाइट है वो टेलीग्राम पर हम पोस्ट कर चुके हैं, तो फटाफट आप डिस्क्रिप्शन बॉक्स खोलकर टेलीग्राम चैनल को ज्वाइन कर लें। वहां पर सभी टीमों के लाइव प्रैक्टिस गेम भी चलते हैं, इसके साथ ही हर मैच की हाईलाइट सब कुछ वहां पर प्रोवाइड कर रहे टेलीग्राम पर। इंट्रा स्क्वाड मुकाबले भी देखने को मिलेंगे तो डिस्क्रिप्शन बॉक्स खोलकर आप टेलीग्राम चैनल पर पहुंच जाएं। फिर रोहित की टीम टारगेट का पीछा करने आई थी। रोहित की तरफ से यहां पर रोहित शर्मा ने बेहतरीन शुरुआत दी, नमन धीर ने उनके साथ ओपन किया था। नमन धीर ने 27 गेंदों में 51 रन बनाए, जबकि रोहित शर्मा यहां पर 43 गेंदों में 95 रन पर नाबाद थे जहां पर एक छक्का तो 121 मीटर का रोहित ने लगाया था। अपनी स्क्रीन पर देख पा रहे होंगे, इसके साथ ही दानिश मेलवार ने नाबाद 19 गेंदों में 34 रन बनाकर फिनिशिंग टचेस दी थी तो रोहित शर्मा 11 ने 199 रन चार विकेट पर केवल 17.5 ओवर में ही स्कोर कर लिया था। अभी विदेशी खिलाड़ियों ने टीमों को ज्वाइन नहीं किया है, केवल इंडियन प्लेयर इस मुकाबले का भाग हैं। इसके साथ ही रघु शर्मा ने तीन विकेट लिए यहां पर चार ओवर में 31 रन देकर। इसके साथ ही अश्विनी कुमार ने 23 रन देकर दो विकेट लिए और मोहम्मद इजहार ने बेहतरीन गेंदबाजी करी 21 रन देकर तीन विकेट चार ओवर में लिए थे, तो इस प्रकार से ये मुकाबला था। इस मुकाबले की कंप्लीट हाईलाइट हमने टेलीग्राम पर डाल दी है और भी बाकी टीमों के जो प्रैक्टिस चल रही है वो सब कुछ टेलीग्राम पर हम प्रोवाइड कर रहे हैं तो आप फटाफट टेलीग्राम चैनल को ज्वाइन कर लें और आप कमेंट करके बताइए और कौन सी टीमों की आप इंफॉर्मेशन जानना चाहते हो।

title: CSK Intra Squad Practice Match 2026 || CSK Practice Match 2026 Highlight | CSK Practice Today
transcription: दोस्तों, IPL 2024 के एडिशन के लिए अभी चल रहे प्रैक्टिस कैंप में चेन्नई की टीम ने आज इंट्रा-स्क्वाड प्रैक्टिस मुकाबला खेला था जहाँ पर MS Dhoni 11 बनाकर और ऋतुराज गायकवाड 11 बनाकर यहाँ पर प्रैक्टिस मुकाबला खेला गया था, जहाँ पर MSD 11 ने पहले टॉस जीतकर गेंदबाजी का फैसला किया था, ऋतु 11 को यहाँ पर पहले बल्लेबाजी कराई थी जहाँ पर ऋतुराज गायकवाड 11 से पहले गायकवाड ने यहाँ पर ओपन किया था, उनके साथ अरावली अवनीश पटेल ने ओपन किया था। दोनों ने ताबड़तोड़ शुरुआत करी जहाँ पर गायकवाड ने 30 गेंदों में 59 रन की बेहतरीन पारी खेली थी, इसके साथ ही यहाँ पर अरावली पटेल ने यहाँ पर 39 गेंदों में 90 रन की विस्फोटक पारी खेली थी। संजू सैमसन नंबर तीन पर आये थे, 18 गेंदों में 46 रन इन्होने बनाए थे, इसके साथ ही यहाँ पर घोष ने, रामकेश घोष ने यहाँ पर 18 रन 10 गेंदों में बनाए थे, इसके साथ ही 28 रन देकर एक विकेट भी लिया था, इसके साथ ही मुकेश चौधरी ने 32 रन देकर एक विकेट लिया था। श्रेयस गोपाल ने यहाँ पर 39 रन देकर तीन विकेट लिए थे और ऋतुराज गायकवाड 11 ने 20 ओवर में 226 रन 8 विकेट पर बनाए थे, बड़ा स्कोर बनाया था। MSD 11 जब टारगेट का यहाँ पर पीछा करने आई तो इनकी भी शुरुआत बेहतरीन रही थी जहाँ पर आयुष माथुर और सरफराज की बेहतरीन ओपनिंग जोड़ी थी। आयुष माथुर ने 45 रन 20 गेंदों में बनाए थे, सरफराज ने 40 गेंदों में 90 रन की पारी खेली थी। विस्फोटक ओपनिंग साझेदारी थी, जबकि यहाँ पर कार्तिक शर्मा नंबर तीन पर आये थे, 12 गेंदों में 30 रन इन्होने बनाए थे और एम एस धोनी ने यहाँ पर 45 रन 20 गेंदों में नाबाद पारी खेली थी, इसके साथ ही प्रशांत वीर भी 35 रन 16 गेंदों में बनाकर नाबाद रहे थे और 19.1 ओवर में 227 रन 5 विकेट पर बनाकर MSD 11 ने ये मुकाबला जीत लिया था जहाँ पर खलील अहमद ने 30 रन देकर दो विकेट लिए थे। राहुल चाहर ने 28 रन देकर चार विकेट लिए थे, इसके साथ ही इस मुकाबले की जो कम्पलीट 10 मिनट की हाईलाइट है वो हम टेलीग्राम पर डाल चुके हैं। बाकी टीमों की भी जो रोज़ इंट्रा-स्क्वाड प्रैक्टिस मुकाबले हो रहे हैं, सारी हाईलाइट्स टेलीग्राम पर आ रही हैं। टेलीग्राम पर लाइव मुकाबले भी आ रहे हैं तो आप फटाफट डिस्क्रिप्शन बॉक्स खोलकर टेलीग्राम चैनल को ज्वाइन कर लें, इसके साथ ही आप कमेंट करके बताइए आप कौन सी title: Marco Rubio Rails Against 'Globalist Bureaucrats' At ICC And 'So-Called International Law'
transcription: For 250 years, Americans have governed ourselves as a free and sovereign people. We choose our own leaders, we determine our own laws, and when we're accused of a crime, we stand for judgment before a jury of our own peers. This is the essential and indispensable feature of our form of government. It is the foundation of our shared way of life. But today, powerful people in faraway places want to take that away from us. They believe that they should be in charge of your laws, of your country, your life, and they don't care whether or not you agree. Halfway across the world, there's an institution that calls itself the International Criminal Court. Maybe you've heard of it, maybe you haven't. But chances are you don't know the names of its judges, of its prosecutors, or its president, and you shouldn't have to. But as we speak, the ICC and its friends are waging a war against our country, not with bullets or missiles, but with statutes and compacts and the force of so-called international law. When the ICC was born 24 years ago, they told us that it was merely a narrow backstop, a global court that would step in to prosecute only the gravest offenses, things like genocide and war crimes, and only when a nation's courts were unable to prosecute them on their own. But the truth is, it was something far more radical and extreme. It was a global tribunal staffed by unelected globalist bureaucrats who claim their power is almost unlimited. The danger of this global court has only continued to grow. Today, it threatens every aspect of our political and legal system. Border patrol agents removing violent criminals from our country, American Marines risking their lives to defend our homeland, prosecutors working to dismantle terrorist plots to attack and kill Americans. If we stand idle, all of them would be at the mercy of foreign judges thousands of miles away, facing the constant risk of prosecution and even imprisonment for the so-called crime of defending their own country. The American people never agreed to any of this, and they never will. Read the words of our Declaration of Independence. We fought a revolution against a foreign power transporting us beyond seas to be tried for pretended offenses. Independence is our birthright. We will never let foreign bureaucrats take that away from us. This administration will not sit by as the ICC and its allies seek to threaten our people. If they believe they can deprive us of our sovereignty, we will teach them the full meaning of American resolve.

transcription: Hi everyone, my name is Alex Sierra and on behalf of myself and Alex Pinto, my co-presenter, I want to talk to you about a session CLS W09: The Impact of Security Usability Challenges in Cloud Environments. The point of this talk is we're going to be looking at a dataset that involves security posture checks on a variety of cloud providers, especially the hyperscalers: AWS, Azure, GCP, and OCI (Oracle Cloud Infrastructure). And we're going to correlate the UX decisions that they have made in the way that users can set up infrastructure, can set up credentials, can set up storage, with security outcomes. We're going to see how much, and if and how much, the way that the cloud providers decided to design their UI and their architecture are leading users to make more or less security mistakes. We feel like this is important for cloud providers and for people designing systems in general to understand the impact of their user experience design in security. Plus, we provide a series of practical recommendations for organizations, for companies, in the way that they use those cloud providers to minimize the impacts that those UX decisions have on their security posture. title: How to Create a Journal System in Joplin | Quick Guide 2026
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: In today's video, I'm going to teach you how to create a journal system in Joplin. Joplin is a fantastic open source note-taking app that offers a lot of flexibility and customization for keeping track of your thoughts, goals, and reflections. Whether you're an avid journaler or looking to start this beneficial habit, Joplin can help you organize your entries in a way that makes them easy to manage and review. Let's start by setting up your journal notebook. To begin, you'll need to open Joplin desktop. Once you have the application up and running, take a look at the left sidebar. You'll find a button labeled "New notebook." Go ahead and click on that. A prompt will appear asking you to enter a name for your new notebook. In this case, you should name it simply "Journal." Naming your notebook distinctly helps maintain clarity and keeps everything organized as your digital journal grows. Now that you have your journal notebook created, you can start thinking about how to organize your entries effectively. A well-structured journal system can provide insights and make reference easier over time. One effective way to structure your journal notebook is to create subnotebooks for different aspects of your journaling practice. To do this, look at the file above your journal notebook. There, you will see an option to create a "new subnotebook." For starters, you might want to create a subnotebook titled "Daily entries." This section will be where you jot down your thoughts and reflections every day. It's a space for freeform writing, capturing everything from daily events to personal reflections. Next, consider adding a subnotebook for "Weekly reviews." This section is great for reflecting on the week that just passed. It offers a valuable opportunity to see how your thoughts and experiences have evolved over the past seven days, and help set intentions for the following week. Finally, there's the "Monthly reviews" subnotebook. Monthly reviews are vital for looking at the bigger picture. They allow you to track longer-term goals and assess progress over time. Reflecting monthly provides a macro perspective of your life, habits, and achievements. When you envision this structure in Joplin, it might look like a tree, with "Journal" as the trunk, "Daily entries," "Weekly reviews," and "Monthly reviews" act as the branches extending from it, providing a clear pathway for your thoughts to spread. By organizing your journal in this manner, you create a harmonious and systematic approach that enhances your journaling practice. This customized structure caters to different aspects of life reflection, and makes it simpler for you to navigate through your thoughts and feelings. Once everything is set up, you can start using Joplin to capture your life's details, review your growth, and make journaling an enriching experience.

title: Diary Entry I Wanted To Share With ALL Footballers...
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: I wanted to share with you guys a diary entry that I wrote during a time that felt like nothing was going smoothly. And you might want to save this video for later because someday you're going to need it. Recently, I've been questioning why nothing in my life seems to be going smoothly. I've been playing football at a high level for years, training harder than everybody else, taking it more seriously than ever before. And still, I'm sitting here with no confirmed answer about where I'm playing next season. Football is competitive, I understand. I have been trying to get my European visa for the past year. I made three different applications and eventually left the country hopeless. And just two days after leaving, they called me for the acceptance meeting. Just two days after I'm out of the country, probably just bad timing, right? I graduated school with a top 1% mark, went to the best university in my country, signed with a professional club, and made a system so strong it changed the lives of 300 players remotely worldwide. And yet, parents are still skeptical to work with me and delay for months just to say no. Probably just a bad coincidence, right? This might be unrelated, but I even approached a trusted brand of dental braces, and halfway through the treatment, I was the first client in company history who had manufacturing issues, so I had to restart the process. And when they sent me the new one, the package got held at customs, and now I have no idea where the $4,000 worth of dental braces are. Just simple procedures that were initially planned to run smoothly and take a few months to complete are now becoming a headache because it's taking a few years to overcome. This is the side of football, the side of life that nobody ever talks about. Every single year without fail, I go through a season like this, a stretch where nothing seems to click, where it feels like the universe itself has turned against me. And here's the lesson I learned from this and what I wanted to share with you guys today. The toughest battles in life are given to the strongest warriors, not because life is cruel but because life is precise. The moment you decide to achieve something amazing, the moment you decide to become a professional footballer, the universe will place you in difficult situations to see what you're made of, to see whether you'll push through to the other side or whether you'll make excuses, blame the system, and quietly walk away from your dream like most people do. Most footballers quit before the breakout even happens, not because they weren't talented enough but because they stopped one season too early. And here's a harsh truth: for the majority of your life, you're going to be in the fight, you're going to be grinding, uncertain if it's going to work out, waiting for the right moment, pushing through the season when nothing feels fair. And then all of a sudden, for a small percentage of your life, everything is going to start to click. You're going to be playing your best football, your confidence is going to be untouchable, the doors are going to start opening up. And that moment right there, that moment is only beautiful because of everything that came before it. The goal in football or in life is not to avoid the hard season. The goal is to refuse to leave before the season ends. So, if you're in it right now, keep training, keep building, keep showing up every single day for your standards when everything around you feels like it's not. You will only fail the moment you decide to quit, and that's a guarantee. So, do not stop and keep pushing till the end.

title: How to Create a Line of Credit Account in QuickBooks Online (Step-By-Step) [2026 guide]
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: In today's video, I'm going to teach you how to create a line of credit account in QuickBooks Online. Having a line of credit account set up in QuickBooks is essential for tracking borrowed funds and repayments accurately within your financial records. Whether you're managing a small business or keeping personal finances in order, this process will help you stay organized and ensure your books are complete and up to date. If you don't already have a QuickBooks Online account, you can use the link in the description to sign up and get started. Now, let's dive into the steps. First, start by logging into your QuickBooks Online account and navigating to your dashboard. Look to the top right corner of the screen where you'll see a small gear icon. This is your settings menu. Go ahead and click on it to open the options. From the dropdown menu that appears, you'll need to scroll down and select the option labeled "Chart of accounts." This is where all your accounts are managed and organized within QuickBooks. Once you're on the chart of accounts page, look towards the upper right corner of the screen again and click the button labeled "New." This will allow you to create a new account. Next, you'll need to enter a name for the account you're setting up. You can choose something straightforward like "Line of Credit," or use a name that better suits your specific needs. It's helpful to pick a name that makes the account easily recognizable when you're reviewing your records later. After naming the account, it's time to assign the correct account type. In the dropdown menu for account type, select "Long-term Liabilities." This category is appropriate because a line of credit typically represents a financial obligation that spans longer than a year. Once you've set the account type, move to the detail type field. From this list, choose "Notes Payable." This detail type is the most accurate for a line of credit, as it represents loans or borrowings that need to be repaid. Finally, click the "Save" button to complete the process and create your new line of credit account. Once saved, the account will appear in your chart of accounts list, and you'll be able to use it to track transactions related to your line of credit. And that's it! You've successfully created a line of credit account in QuickBooks Online. If you found this video helpful, please like and subscribe.

title: Video 3: Why is sharing your radiotherapy treatment story important to you?
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: It's been really important to me all along to share my story of my treatment, my diagnosis, my treatment and my recovery, to whoever will listen, to be perfectly honest. My first desire was to tell fellow patients, and I was interviewed by a radiation oncologist. My answers to my, her questions were recorded, and those videos have been shared by doctors and other cancer team members to thousands of people who've been diagnosed with a head and neck cancer. And I'm just so grateful that clinicians have seen the value of sharing a patient's story. I think there's no substitute for a patient who's about to have radiotherapy to hear the story of a fellow patient, not only just describe what the treatment's like and the recovery's like, but just to see a patient who's survived, who's survived cancer. Because I think so many of us when we get that cancer diagnosis, we're just full of anxiety and fear, and there's nothing as reassuring as seeing a patient who's gone through it and come out the other side. But I also think it's good for cancer team members to see these videos because it, it exposes them to the emotional and psychological impact of a cancer diagnosis and the treatment. And if they can hear the patient's story, empathize, uh, understand emotionally, feel some of those feelings, I think they're much more likely to do research and make an effort to help us psychologically, which I think is as important as survival.

title: Blue Monday
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription:
Let's talk therapy. My name is Rafal Kolary from Edinburgh Taxi Therapy.

Blue Monday, it is a concept that the third Monday of January, it's been named the most depressing day of the year. This is the time when people usually struggle with paying the bills, as well as they struggle with the New Year's Eve resolution and how December went for them.

After Christmas, after New Year's Eve, we feel that our motivation is a little bit lower. Then, when we look outside, the weather, it's not the best one. This is not Gran Canaria, Tenerife or any other hot spot. It's Scotland. It's raining, it's gloomy, and we are affected by that.

Money pressure have huge impact on how we feel. Obviously, the Christmas finished, the New Year's Eve is over. We are back to reality. We are back to making sure that we need to cover our daily expectations, have enough money for food, have enough money for our life, and then the money are not coming because it's still almost middle of January. That's when the anxiety, low mood, depression might come to the picture.

In regards to seeking the support, you might feel that your mood is low, the anxiety is there. You do not feel well about yourself, and your self-esteem is being affected. However, you do not have to wait for the crisis to kick in. Sometimes it's better to work with the prevention. It's better to make sure that everything is fine. This is the perfect moment to look for the support.

It's important to find a space, a safe space, confidential one, where you would be able to explore your feelings and understand what is going on in your life.

My personal reflection in regards of the Blue Monday is, this is the moment when it's time to get out from the house. It is the moment to introduce some exercises, enjoy the sun while you can catch it, spend some times with your friends, and if this doesn't help, maybe look for the support like Edinburgh Taxi Therapy, or any other psychologists which are available in your neighborhood.

title: The Bright Side of AI
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: With all the AI gloom and doom, I often forget how cool AI actually is. Like, what a technology, what a time to be alive. You know, like, I often have this heaviness about it, and more of this, "I gotta use this. I gotta make this work. I need to catch up with with the trends and everything, not to fall behind." And what I lose sight of sometimes is how amazing this technology is, and I just, today, I had this case of, hey, you can, you can use AI to analyze your thought patterns, like your personal thought patterns, and not only can you understand how you think, but obviously also where your blind spots are, and and how you can improve your thinking, and how, what are, what the patterns are, and this, getting this awareness about yourself, in all kinds of areas, obviously professionally, how you make decisions, but but also in private, it's such an amazing feat, to be honest. This technology didn't exist. Like, how would you else, like, get to this? Like, of course, if you do therapy for 10 years, which nobody wants, and and I'm not really a fan of it, still, there's this other person processing it, and you probably not get to the root of it. Now, you can upload hours, hundreds of hours of you interacting in in Zoom calls, whatever it is, and you can have AI analyze, find out your thought patterns, even like making your thoughts visible to yourself. And I just thought, how amazing, and this is just one use case, obviously. There's so much to be had also with this technology. It's scary. It's It puts a pressure on myself, and I guess on you as well, but it's also fabulous, and this is my, my little reminder to myself, and maybe to you, that if you, if you set aside this, this pressure, this, this fear maybe even, and and let in the, the possibilities and the opportunity a little bit more, it could be tremendously fun to interact with this technology, and and all the, the beautiful things that can come from that. title: You Don’t Have To Be Okay Right Now (Listen to This)

transcription: Hey, I don't know what you're going through right now, but I have a feeling it's been heavy, not just one thing, but everything at once. And I know your mind might not stop going over the same thoughts again and again, thinking about everything that could go wrong or everything you wish you did differently, but not every thought you have is telling you the truth. Sometimes, your mind is just exhausted. So, just for a second, take a breath with me, slowly in and out. You don't need to fix your whole life tonight. You don't need to solve everything all at once, just focus on this moment, just getting through right now, that's enough. And even if it doesn't feel like it, you're doing better than you think. You've made it through days that felt impossible before. You're still here, and that matters more than you realize. So, if today felt like too much, if you felt overwhelmed, if you felt like you were falling behind, just know this, you're not alone in that feeling, and you don't have to carry it all perfectly. You don't have to be okay, you just have to keep going, one moment at a time.

title: Are You Okay... Really?
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: We ask it out of habit every single day, but we rarely listen for the truth. "How are you? Are you okay?" "Yeah, I'm fine." It's the ultimate American defense mechanism. We live in a culture that glorifies the grind, praises independence, and tells us to "fake it till we make it." So when things get heavy, our language shrinks. We reduce an entire ocean of burnout, anxiety, and quiet exhaustion into a single automatic wall. "Have you been crying?" "No, just tired." "Just tired." It's the perfect cover-up. Because nobody questions it. In a world where everyone is exhausted, it's easy to hide. But there's a massive difference between needing sleep and being tired of waking up feeling empty. Depression doesn't always look like tears or dramatic breakdowns. In reality, it looks like complete isolation. It's sitting in a crowded room in New York or a quiet suburb in Ohio, surrounded by people, yet feeling entirely invisible. It's building walls so high that even the people who love you can't reach you. "Do you want to talk about it? You can tell me anything." "No, there's nothing to talk about." When someone pushes you away, it's rarely a rejection. Most of the time, they literally just don't have the words. How do you explain a profound sadness that has no specific cause? How do you tell your family or your friends that your life looks great on paper, but feels completely hollow inside? So they say "No," hoping you'll leave them alone, but secretly praying that you won't. They don't need a lecture, they don't need a motivational speech, toxic positivity, or a 10-step plan on how to fix their life. "Do you want a hug?" "Yeah." Sometimes saving a life doesn't take a hero, it doesn't take the perfect words. It just takes the willingness to sit in the dark with someone. The most powerful thing you can say to someone who is drowning isn't "I understand." It's simply, "I'm here, and you don't have to carry this alone." Right now, millions of people are fighting battles they don't talk about. And ironically, the people who spend all their energy checking on everyone else are often the ones drowning the fastest. Do me a favor today. Don't just send a casual text asking "How's it going?" Call someone, look them in the eyes, break through the automatic answers. Because you never truly know how heavy a burden is until you offer to help hold it. Check on your people today.

title: Inside the Mind of Someone Who Feels Alone | Deep Narration About Loneliness
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Sometimes the loneliest feeling isn't when you're alone, it's when you're surrounded by people and still feel like you don't belong. The room is full of voices, laughter, conversations, noise, but somehow, none of it reaches you. You smile when they look at you, you nod like you're listening, you say you're fine, because it's easier than explaining what's going on inside your head. Sometimes you hold your phone, staring at the screen, wanting to text someone, but not knowing who would understand. You start typing, then delete everything, because how do you explain a feeling you don't even understand yourself? Outside, the world keeps moving. People walk with purpose, cars pass by. Everyone seems to be going somewhere. And you wonder why you feel stuck in the same place, every single day. Loneliness isn't always silence. Sometimes it's noise that doesn't include you. Sometimes it's laughing with people, but feeling nothing inside. Sometimes it's going home and realizing, no one really knows how you feel. You sit in your room, the lights are off. The only sound is your own thoughts, and they don't stop. You ask yourself questions: Why do I feel like this? Why can't I connect? Why does everything feel so far away? But even on days like this, when the silence feels too loud, a small part of you is still there. Still breathing, still trying, still hoping. And sometimes, that's enough. Sometimes, making it through the day while feeling alone is already a victory. And maybe tomorrow feels lighter. Maybe not easier, but a little less heavy. title: How To Create a Winning Pitch Deck | Experienced Voices
transcription: Hello, I'm Jean Gray, publisher of American Entrepreneurship Today. Welcome to this special video tutorial from our Experienced Voices podcast series. A great pitch deck doesn't just show data. It tells a compelling story. It is the single most important asset you have when raising capital. Today we're breaking down the eight essential elements that captivate investors and turn that maybe into a yes. Let's dive in. Every successful company starts by identifying a genuine pain point. Don't just list facts, tell a story. Who is hurting and why is the current way of doing things broken? Make the investor feel the friction of the status quo. If they don't feel the pain, they won't value your medicine. Now present your solution. This is where you introduce your product or service as a hero of the story. Focus on the benefits, the so what, not just the technical features. Show, don't tell. A quick demo or a high-quality product render works best here to make your vision feel real. Investors want to back big wins. This is your chance to show the scale of the opportunity. Clearly define your TAM, your SAM, and your SOM. Use credible third-party data to prove that this market is not only large but growing. Prove that this is a venture-scale opportunity worth their time. How do you turn this into a profitable machine? Briefly explain your revenue model. But more importantly, show your traction. Whether it's user growth, pilot programs, or revenue milestones, show that your theory has been validated by the market. Traction is the ultimate risk reducer. Never say you have no competition. It implies you haven't done your research. Acknowledge the landscape, then clearly articulate your unfair advantage, or moat. Why are you different, and why is that difference defensible? Focus on why you win, not just where they fall short. Investors bet on jockeys, not just on horses. Highlight why your team has the unique expertise to execute this vision. Then pivot to the ask. Be transparent. How much are you raising, and what specific milestones will this capital unlock? Be confident, clear, and focused on the future. Finally, wrap up with a summary of your vision. One powerful sentence that captures the future you're building. Thank your audience, and leave them with a clear next step, whether that's your website, an email link, or a direct invite to a demo. The deck is your foot in the door. title: The Perfect 60-Second Startup Pitch (Investors Will Remember)
transcription: The perfect 60-second startup pitch. Imagine you step into an elevator with your dream investor. You have exactly 60 seconds before the doors open. Would you know what to say? Most founders make one big mistake. They try to explain everything about their business. The truth is, your goal isn't to close the investment in 60 seconds. It's to make the investor want another conversation. Here's a simple framework that works. First, start with the problem. What pain are you solving? Keep it simple and relatable. If the investor doesn't understand the problem, they won't care about the solution. Next, explain your solution. In one sentence, describe what your company does. Avoid technical jargon or long explanations. If someone outside your industry can't understand it, it's probably too complicated. Then, explain why now. Why is this the right time for your business? Maybe a new technology has made your solution possible. Maybe customer behavior has changed. Maybe the market is growing rapidly. Investors want to know why this opportunity exists today, not 5 years ago. After that, share your traction. You don't need millions in revenue, but you do need evidence that you're making progress. That could be paying customers, user growth, partnerships, pilot programs, or even a growing waitlist. Traction reduces uncertainty and builds confidence. Finally, finish with the opportunity. Don't end by asking for money. Instead, leave the investor wanting to learn more. Give them a reason to schedule a second meeting. Remember, a great pitch doesn't answer every question. It answers just enough to create curiosity. If an investor walks away wanting to know more, you've done your job. The best founders don't overwhelm investors with information. They tell a clear story, communicate confidence, and make their business easy to understand. Because at the end of the day, investors don't invest in the longest pitch, they invest in the clearest one.
