transcription: റെഡ് ക്രോസ്സ് സൊസൈറ്റി എന്നാണ് IRCS ൻ്റെ പൂർണ്ണരൂപം. അടുത്തത് ICRC, ഇതിൻ്റെ പൂർണ്ണരൂപം എന്താണ്? ICRC യുടെ പൂർണ്ണരൂപം എന്താണ്? ഉത്തരം, International Committee of the Red Cross, എന്താണ്, International Committee of the Red Cross, ICRC-യുടെ പൂർണ്ണരൂപം ഇതാണ്, International Committee of the Red Cross. മറന്നുപോകരുത്, IRCS - Indian Red Cross Society, ICRC - International Committee of the Red Cross. അടുത്ത ചോദ്യം, സ്കൂളുകളിൽ ജൂനിയർ റെഡ് ക്രോസ്സിന് ഗ്രേസ് മാർക്ക് അനുവദിക്കാൻ തുടങ്ങിയ വർഷം? സ്കൂളുകളിൽ ജൂനിയർ റെഡ് ക്രോസ്സിന് ഗ്രേസ് മാർക്ക് അനുവദിക്കാൻ തുടങ്ങിയ വർഷം? ഉത്തരം വരുന്നത് 2005. 2005 ലാണ് സ്കൂളുകളിൽ ജൂനിയർ റെഡ് ക്രോസ്സിന് ഗ്രേസ് മാർക്ക് അനുവദിക്കാൻ തുടങ്ങിയത്. ഏത് വർഷമാണ്? 2005ൽ. അടുത്തത്, റെഡ് ക്രോസ്സ് സൊസൈറ്റിയുടെ പ്രധാന പ്രമേയം അല്ലെങ്കിൽ മുദ്രാവാക്യം എന്താണ്? റെഡ് ക്രോസ്സ് സൊസൈറ്റിയുടെ പ്രധാന പ്രമേയം അല്ലെങ്കിൽ മുദ്രാവാക്യം എന്താണ്? ഉത്തരം സർവീസ്, സേവനമാണ് റെഡ് ക്രോസ്സ് സൊസൈറ്റിയുടെ പ്രധാന പ്രമേയം. അപ്പൊ ഫ്രണ്ട്സ് ഈയൊരു വീഡിയോ നിങ്ങൾക്കെല്ലാവർക്കും യൂസ്ഫുൾ ആയെന്ന് കരുതുന്നു. JRC യുമായി ബന്ധപ്പെട്ട അടിസ്ഥാന വിവരങ്ങളാണ് നമ്മൾ നോക്കിയത്. എക്സാമിന് ചോദിക്കാൻ സാധ്യതയുള്ള കുറച്ചു ചോദ്യങ്ങളാണിത്. അപ്പൊ നമുക്കിനി നിങ്ങൾക്കായുള്ള സ്പെഷ്യൽ ക്വസ്റ്റ്യൻ നോക്കാം. ചോദ്യമിതാണ് ലോക റെഡ് ക്രോസ്സ് ദിനം എന്നാണ്? ലോക റെഡ് ക്രോസ്സ് ദിനം എന്നാണ് ആചരിക്കുന്നത്? അപ്പൊ ഈ ചോദ്യത്തിന്റെ ഉത്തരം ഇപ്പൊ എല്ലാവർക്കും കിട്ടിയിട്ടുണ്ടാവും. അവരെന്ത് ചെയ്യുക? പെട്ടെന്ന് തന്നെ അത് കമൻറ് ബോക്സിൽ രേഖപ്പെടുത്തുക. ഒപ്പം നിങ്ങളുടെ പേരും കൂടി ആഡ് ചെയ്യാൻ മറക്കണ്ട. പ്രധാനപ്പെട്ട ചോദ്യമാണ് എല്ലാവരും അറിഞ്ഞിരിക്കേണ്ടതാണ്. അറിയാത്തവർ എന്താ ചെയ്യാ? പെട്ടെന്ന് തന്നെ പോയി ആ ചോദ്യത്തിന്റെ ഉത്തരം നോക്കി പഠിച്ചു വയ്ക്കുക കേട്ടോ. അപ്പൊ ഇതുപോലെ നിങ്ങൾക്ക് കൂടുതൽ വീഡിയോസ് ആവശ്യമാണെങ്കിൽ ചാനൽ മറക്കാതെ ഒന്ന് സബ്സ്ക്രൈബ് ചെയ്തു വച്ചോളൂ, ബെൽ ഐക്കണും എനേബിൾ ചെയ്യാൻ മറക്കണ്ട. ഈ വീഡിയോ നിങ്ങൾക്ക് യൂസ്ഫുൾ ആയിട്ടുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ നിങ്ങളുടെ ഫ്രണ്ട്സിലേക്കും ഷെയർ ചെയ്തു കൊടുത്തോളൂ. വീഡിയോ ലൈക് ചെയ്യാനും സബ്സ്ക്രൈബ് ചെയ്യാനും മറക്കരുത്. താങ്ക് യു ഫോർ വാച്ചിങ്.

title: 10th Class Ia-1 Sanskrit Real Question Paper 2026। Class 9 Internal assessment-1 Sanskrit Question।
transcription: ଭିତର ଦେଲାଟାରେ? ବୋପଦେବଃ ପ୍ରଥମତଃ କିମ, ବୋପଦେବଃ ପ୍ରଥମତଃ କିମ ପଢିତୁମ ଆଚରଣବାନ, ଓକେ। ତ ଏଇଟା ହବ କଣ ନା ପ୍ରଥମ ହେଇଯିବ ବୈଦେଶିକ ବନ୍ତଃ ତମାନଙ୍କର ହେଇଯିବ କରେକ୍ଟ ଆନସର। ନେକ୍ସ୍ଟ ରହିବ ତମାନଙ୍କର ୟୁନିଟ-3 ର ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ, ୟୁନିଟ-3 ର ପ୍ରଶ୍ନରେ ଦେଲା ଉପମନ୍ୟୁଃ କ୍ଷୁଧାର୍ତ୍ତଃ ଓକେ ସନ କଣ ଖାଇଦେଲେ? ନା ଉପମନ୍ୟୁଃ କ୍ଷୁଧାର୍ତ୍ତଃ ତତ୍ କାନି ଅଭକ୍ଷୟତ୍ ଉପ ଉପମନ୍ୟୁ ଭୋକରେ କଣ ଖାଇଦେଇଥିଲେ ନା ଅର୍କପତ୍ରାଣି ବା ଅରଖ ଲେଖିଦଉଛି ଏଠାରେ ଅରଖ ପତ୍ର। ଉପମନ୍ୟୁ ଭୋକରେ କଣ ଖାଇଦେଇଥିଲେ ପିଲାମାନେ? ନା ଅରଖ ପତ୍ର। ନେକ୍ସ୍ଟ ରହିଲା ତମାନଙ୍କର କଥମ ଉପମନ୍ୟୁଃ, କଥମ ଉପମନ୍ୟୁଃ ଆ କଣ ଅଛି ନାଗଛତ୍ ଓକେ? ତ କଥମ ଉପମନ୍ୟୁଃ ଆଶ୍ରମ ନାଗଛତ୍, ଏଇଟା ତ ପିଲାମାନେ କରିପାରିବ। ନେକ୍ସ୍ଟ ରହିବ ତମାନଙ୍କର ତିନି ନମ୍ବର ଓକେ, କ୍ୟା ପ୍ରୀତି ଅସ୍ମାତ୍, ଓକେ। ଏଇଟା ତମାନଙ୍କର ଗୁରୁଭକ୍ତିହାଃ, ଗୁରୁ ଲେଖିଦଉଛି ପିଲାମାନେ, ଆନସର ଗୁଡିକ ମୁଁ ଏଠି କହିଦଉଛି ଗୁରୁଭକ୍ତିହାଃ। ପିଲାମାନେ, ମେମ୍ବରସିପରେ ସବୁ ଅଲରେଡି ଆପଲୋଡ ହେଇସାରିଲାଣି, ୫୦ ରୁ ଉର୍ଦ୍ଧ ପିଲାମାନେ ବର୍ତ୍ତମାନ ନେଇସାରିଲେଣି ଓକେ। ତମାନେ ଯାଇ ଦେଖି ମଧ୍ୟ ପାର। ଯଥାଶୀଘ୍ର ଜଏନ ଅପସନ ଉପରେ କ୍ଲିକ କର, ଆଉ ବେଶୀ କିଛି ଡେରି କରନି। ଜଏନ ଅପସନ ଉପରେ କ୍ଲିକ କରି ପିଲାମାନେ ବହୁତ କମ ପ୍ରାଇଜ ଅଛି, ତମାନେ ମେମ୍ବରସିପ ପିଲାମାନେ ଲେଖିଦଉଛି ଏଠାରେ, ମେମ୍ବରସିପ ପିଲାମାନେ ନେଇଯାଅ। ବହୁତ କମ ପ୍ରାଇଜ ତମାନଙ୍କର ରହିଛି। ନେକ୍ସ୍ଟ ରହିବ ତମାନଙ୍କର ନୈତତ୍ ଓକେ। ଏଇଟା ସନ୍ଧିବିଛେଦ କଲେ କଣ ହବ ଇତି? ଏଇଟା କଣ ହବରେ ପିଲାମାନେ ନ ଯୁକ୍ତ ଏତତ୍, ନ ଯୁକ୍ତ ଏତତ୍ ତମେ ଏଠାରେ କରିପାରିବ। ନେକ୍ସ୍ଟ ରହିବ ତମାନଙ୍କର ଚାରି ନମ୍ବର ଦେଲା ମାତୃଭାଷାୟା ତମାନଙ୍କର ସ୍ଵମାତୃଭାଷାୟା ଉତ୍ତରମ ଲିଖତ, ଓକେ। ତ ସ୍ଵମାତୃଭାଷାୟା ନିଜ ମାତୃଭାଷାରେ ଉତ୍ତର ଲେଖିବା। କହ, କହ କବିକୁଳସ୍ୟ ଲଲାଟଃ ମୁକୁଟମଣିଃ? କିଏ କବିକୁଳ ଲଲାଟର ମୁକୁଟମଣି ଅଟନ୍ତି? ଏଠି ତମାନଙ୍କୁ ଲେଖିବାକୁ କୁହାଯାଇଛି। ନେକ୍ସ୍ଟ ଦୁଇ ନମ୍ବର ଦେଲା, ସର୍ବଦମନଃ ଇତି ବାଳସ୍ୟ ନାମ କେନ ଉକ୍ତବାନ? ଓକେ, ତ ସର୍ବଦମନର ଯେଉଁ ନାମ ଦିଆଯାଇଥିଲା ସର୍ବଦମନ, ଏଇଟା କାହା ମାନଙ୍କ ଦ୍ଵାରା ଦିଆଯାଇଥିଲା, ନା ଋଷିମାନଙ୍କ ଦ୍ଵାରା ଦିଆଯାଇଥିଲା। ନେକ୍ସ୍ଟ ହବ ତମାନଙ୍କର ରକ୍ଷାକରଣ୍ଡକେ କା କୋ ସିଦ୍ଧଃ ଅସ୍ତି? ରକ୍ଷାକରଣ୍ଡକରେ କୋଉ ପ୍ରକାର ଔଷଧ ଥିଲା ତମାନଙ୍କର ଏଠାରେ ପିଲାମାନେ କରିପାରିବ। ନେକ୍ସ୍ଟ ହବ ତମାନଙ୍କର IV ରେ, IV ରେ ଦେଲା କସ୍ୟା, କସ୍ୟା ଉଟଜେ ମୃତ୍ତିକା ମୟୂରଃ ଆସୀତ? ଓକେ, କଣ ହବରେ ନା ପ୍ରଥମ ତପସ୍ଵୀ, ଯେଉଁ ମୃତ୍ତିକା ମୟୂରଟି ଆଣିବାକୁ ଯାଇଥିଲା କାହାର କୁଟୀରରେ ଥିଲା? ନା ପ୍ରଥମ ତପସ୍ଵୀ କୁଟୀରରେ। ନେକ୍ସ୍ଟ ହବ ତମାନଙ୍କର ଓକେ, ଏଇଟା ତମାନଙ୍କର କଣ ହବ ଭିଟା ସିଂହସ୍ୟ ଗର୍ଜନେନ? ସିଂହସ୍ୟ ଗର୍ଜନେନ ହେଇଯିବ ତମାନଙ୍କର ଲାଷ୍ଟ କରେକ୍ଟ ଆନସର। ତ ଫାଇନାଲି ପିଲାମାନେ ମୁଁ ସବୁ କୋସିନର ୧୦୦ ତୁ ୧୦୦ % କରେକ୍ଟ ଆନସର ଡିସକସନ କଲି, ତମାନଙ୍କର ୧୦୦ % ପିଲାମାନେ ତମାନଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ଏକ୍ଜାମରେ ହେଲ୍ପଫୁଲ ହବ। ସାଙ୍ଗସାଥୀମାନଙ୍କୁ ନିହାତି ଭାବରେ ଶେୟାର କର। ଆଉ ମେମ୍ବରସିପ ନେଇନଥିଲେ ଯଥାଶୀଘ୍ର ଜଏନ ଅପସନ ଉପରେ କ୍ଲିକ କରି ପିଲାମାନେ ମେମ୍ବରସିପ ନେଇଯାଅ। ବହୁତ ପିଲାମାନେ ଅଲରେଡି ମେମ୍ବରସିପ ନେଇସାରିଲେଣି ଓକେ। ତମେମାନେ ମଧ୍ୟ ନେଇଯାଅ। ଓକେ ଥାଙ୍କ ୟୁ ଫର ଵାଚିଙ୍ଗ ଭିଡିଓଟିକୁ କମ୍ପ୍ଲିଟଲି ଵାଚ କରିଥିବାରୁ, ଏତିକିରେ ରହୁଛି ପିଲାମାନେ ଜୟ ଜଗନ୍ନାଥ।

अब तक के आपके टोटल पॉडकास्ट में सबसे ज्यादा झूठ उसी में बोला गया है। और रोशन सर से ही बात पूछते हैं, उन्हें बुरा नहीं लगा तो, जिस समय उनको पॉडकास्ट में आए थे ना, उस समय उनको नेपाल जाना चाहिए था। रोशन रंजन सर के पॉडकास्ट में जिस चीज ने पूरे देश के दिल को झकझोरा था, वो चीज थी जब उन्होंने कहा कि अगर खान सर ने झूठ नहीं बोला होता... ...गोली चला है, 8-10 राउंड तो हम देखे हैं यहाँ पे। एफआईआर नहीं होता, एफआईआर नहीं होता तो मेरा भाई नेपाल नहीं जाता, नेपाल नहीं जाता तो मेरा भाई जिंदा होता। सब कुछ छीन लिया गया खान सर के एक झूठ से। 2 जून को ये स्टेटमेंट नहीं देते कि गोली चला है तो हमारा भाई पटना में ही रहता। क्या हम इतने बेवकूफ हैं जो नेशनल चैनल पे आ के, गोली नहीं चली रहेगी हम बोलेंगे चला है? सिंपैथी होती है कोई चीज, जब कोई जेल चला जाता है या कोई दुर्भाग्यपूर्ण घटना हो जाती है। आप ये कह रहे हैं प्रिंस की मौत के लिए आप जिम्मेदार नहीं हैं? आप बताइए कैसे जिम्मेदार हैं? हम इस घटना का दोषी फैजल खान को मानते हैं सर। क्या हम नेपाल भेजे थे? क्या हम कहे थे की किडनैप करके लाओ? हम बोले थे की नेपाल की शराब लाओ? हम बोले थे की पिस्टल कमर में लेकर घूमो? हम बोले थे की किसी से रंगदारी मांगो? क्या हमने इनके सर पे मारा था? सर ये बहुत सेंसिटिव विषय है क्योंकि प्रिंस अब इस दुनिया में नहीं है। अगर ये फैक्ट गलत होगा... देखिए ये बात बोलना नहीं चाहिए, ये हम कुछ एफआईआर ले आते हैं। प्रिंस के ऊपर दो किडनैपिंग का, तीन-तीन आर्म्स एक्ट का... तो मृतक व्यक्ति के बारे में आप ये बातें क्यों बता रहे हो? क्योंकि उनको पुलिस दूसरे केस में भी ढूंढ रही थी। ये वो एफआईआर है जिसके वजह से देश छोड़ के जाना पड़ा। और इतना ही नहीं एक और केस होता है उसके बाद। और एक चीज वो बहुत बड़ा गलत छुपाए हैं... खान सर पर देश कैसे भरोसा करे जब उनके खानदान के लोग उनपर भरोसा नहीं करते? उनका चाचा उन्हें कह रहा है कि गद्दार आदमी है, बगैरत आदमी है... अरे वो चोटा हमारा चाचा नहीं है, एकदम एक नंबर का फ्रॉडिया आदमी है... अवध ओझा सर, उन्होंने कहा कि आपने एक लाख करोड़ रुपए का नुकसान कर लिया होगा... एक लाख करोड़ से नीचे वो बतियाए नहीं करते हैं। वो राजा बनने का उनका...

title: Khan Sir Breaks Silence| Full Podcast 5PM 18/07/2026 @unpluggedshubhankar
transcription: हिंदी बताते हैं। 2 जून की घटना के बारे में वो लोग ज्ञान दे रहे हैं जो वहां से कई किलोमीटर दूर थे। फिर आपको 40 दिन बाद क्यों बेल मिली? आप तो एंटीसिपेटरी बेल पर बाहर थे। 20 तारीख को हमारी ज़मानत मिल जाती है। हमारी कैसे लेट हो गई, हम बताते हैं। आपके पास दो आधार कार्ड हैं? आप फैज़ल खान के अलावा अमित सिंह भी हो? जबकि हमको ऐसे लोग अमित सिंह कह के बुलाते हैं। लेकिन दो आधार कार्ड है, सर उसका... इसपे तो जा के केस करना है, ज़मानत ख़त्म हो जाएगी। जब आपको पता चला कि रौशन सर जेल में गए, आपने एफ़आईआर क्यों नहीं वापस ली? महामूर्ख, जो कानून नहीं पढ़ा है, वही बोल सकता है। अंजना ओम कश्यप से कहना कि ज़ुबान खींच लेंगे, थूकेंगे, तलवा चाटती हो, ये करती हो, वो करती हो, वो थोड़ा ज़्यादा नहीं था? बेटे का ज़िक्र करना, ये खान सर का बिलो द बेल्ट था? ज़्यादा था ही, उसने भी उधर से बोला था 'दो कौड़ी का'। लेकिन उनके चैनल ने मेरा घर दिखा दिया। मतलब आपकी प्राइवेसी, प्राइवेसी? तो फिर सारे टीचर लोग आपके दुश्मन काहे बन गए? सारे टीचर नहीं, ये 10-15 गो हैं। ये बनना चाहते थे मेरी तरह, नहीं बन पाए, तो उनका खुन्नस है। और सबसे दुःख जानते हैं किस बात का लगा? लोग प्रिंस के लाश के सामने बैठ के उसके गांव में नाच रहे थे। ये गिनवा रहे थे कि खान सर का फीस महंगा है कि सस्ता है। अरे हरामियों, कोई लाश पड़ी है न्याय के लिए सालों, तुम लोग टीचर हो! एक थ्योरी आई थी कि आपको शायद ट्रैप करने के लिए पुलिस या किसी ने... खबर भिजवाया गया ना, कि आपकी मां जो हैं, वो आखरी सांस ले रही हैं, बात कर लीजिए। आज़ाद भारत में पहली बार किसी इंसान को गिरफ्तार करने के लिए इतना जी-जान लगाया गया था। चाहे मीडिया हो, टीचर हो, प्रशासन हो... आप रक्षाबंधन मनाते हैं, त्रिपुंड लगाते हैं, लेकिन ईद नहीं मनाते हैं उस तरह से। और ये सब मार्केटिंग पीआर का हिस्सा होता है... मेरे जीवन में बस एक ही कमी है, कि मेरी बहन नहीं है। तो हम शुरू जब किए थे, तो पांच ही राखी होती थी। ये हज़ार राखी एक दिन में हुई है। एक सवाल आया, खान सर गरीबी बेचते हैं। तो अमीरी बेचें? ये चोट्टा वो कह रहा है जो 4-4 हज़ार में पीडीएफ बेचता है। लोग कहते हैं कि आस्तीन में सांप पाल रहे थे, हम आस्तीन में सूअर पाले थे। आप दिखाते हैं कि आप प्रोग्रेसिव इंसान हैं, लेकिन आप पिछड़ी सोच के आदमी हैं और इस बार भी उनके धर्म का, बुर्के का, ये सारी चीज़ें आई। यार हमको ये नहीं समझ में आता, हमारी मेहरारू को देखने के लिए एकनी को कौन सा चूल मचल रहता है! पाकिस्तान भागने का इरादा तो नहीं था आपका? title: Khan Sir Breaks Silence| Full Podcast 5PM 18/07/2026 @unpluggedshubhankar
transcription: रोल-रोल बड़ा एक बढ़िया किए। तो अंजना जी के नहीं, कंचना जी के फैन हो गए। हां, कंचना जी। अरे महाराज! तेज प्रताप यादव कहे कि हम खान सर का समर्थन नहीं करते, इनको जेल में होना चाहिए। भरोसा है कि ये हत्या करवाया है और उसको जेल जाना चाहिए। जुगनुओं ने पी रखी थी शराब, भर-भर के सूरज को गालियां दी कि तुम क्या ही चमकते हो, हमको देखो, हम क्या चमकते हैं। रोशन सर ने कहा कि हम भी सस्ता पढ़ाते हैं। एक ₹200 का सवाल है सर, हम भी ₹100 में सर पढ़ाते हैं। अभिनय मैथ्स सर ने भी यही जिक्र किया, यही बात अवध ओझा भी कह रहे थे। ये लोग 50 करोड़ जॉइनिंग लेते थे, ये सब लोग अपना पेनड्राइव और रिकॉर्डेड कोर्स हजारों में बेचते थे, लॉकडाउन से पहले। खान सर फर्जी रेवेन्यू ऑफिसर, फर्जी इनकम टैक्स ऑफिसर, फर्जी एयर फोर्स विंग कमांडर, नीरज को वो राफेल उड़वा देते हैं जबकि उसका नाम मेरिट में नहीं है। अब लोग मजाक उड़ा रहे हैं कि नीरज राफेल उड़ा रहा है, सुखोई उड़ा रहा है। जिस नीरज नाम के लड़के का और ये जो रेवेन्यू ऑफिसर था, इनकम टैक्स ऑफिसर था, इसपे हमने केस किया है, ये एक नंबर का धूर्त और कमीना, हरामी आदमी है ये। एक टीचर हैं, जिनके लिए आपने मुखिया चुनाव का प्रचार तक किया था, उन्होंने यूट्यूब पर वीडियो बनाकर सबसे ज्यादा आपको एक्सपोज़ किया। वो 12वीं पढ़ा ऑर्केस्ट्रा में लौंडा नाच करने वाले को हम मुखिया बना दिए, वो भी तो फर्जी रिजल्ट था? कुछ कुत्ते अपने होते हैं और कुछ अपने लोग ही कुत्ते होते हैं। 69वीं बीपीएससी में 400 सिलेक्शन का दावा किया गया था, अब बच्चा लोग पूछ रहा है कि 70वीं बीपीएससी में आपके क्लासरूम कोर्स से कितने बच्चे निकले? और ये 69वीं बीपीएससी वाला 400 सिलेक्शन लोग कह रहे हैं खाली 10 लड़का सिलेक्ट हुआ आपका, बाकी सब नहीं हुआ है। 20,000 टोटल बच्चे हैं, आपने 12,000 दावा कर दिया, रोशन सर ने 10,000 दावा कर दिया, कुल लड़का पास हुआ 19,838। उन्होंने जहां कहा कि 10,000 रिजल्ट, उस बिल्डिंग की कैपेसिटी 3,000 है। कपिल शर्मा, केबीसी हर जगह बताया कि मेरी कोचिंग में बम फेंका गया था। बम-वम मार दिया था सर। हैं? और एक दिन हो गया बम चला दिया गया हमारे यहाँ। अब लड़का लोग कहता है कि बम कांड में आपने एफआईआर करवाई ही नहीं। दो जूता देंगे जो बोला है कि एफआईआर नहीं करवाए, हम क्या उन्होंने कोई केस दर्ज करवाया है? उसको लेकर के उन्होंने कोई केस दर्ज नहीं करवाया है। तुम जाके थाना में पता किया है कि एफआईआर नहीं है? खान सर के कोचिंग में और खान सर के अस्पताल में खाली कैश पेमेंट चलता है जिसके जरिए वो नंबर दो का काम करते हैं। चींटियां तादाद में कितनी भी क्यों ना हों, गन्ना घसीट के नहीं ले जा सकतीं और हम कह देना चाहते हैं कि हम रातों-रात कुकुरमुत्ता की तरह नहीं निकले हैं ज़मीन से कि मसल दिए जाएंगे। ऐसी वीडियो दूसरे टीचरों ने बनाया था, खान सर पढ़ाते थोड़ी हैं, खाली हवाबाजी करते हैं। आप पढ़ाते हो अभी भी? क्या बात करते हैं। हम पूछ रहे हैं भाई, हमको क्लास में कोई नाचता है, मुजरा करता है क्लास में? एक आरोप जो सबने लगाया कि बहुत सारे टीचर्स को विवेक बिंद्रा के जरिए

title: Investigation uncovers sexual abuse allegations against Cesar Chavez
transcription: suggestions that sex played a role in his efforts to control the movement at a period of time in particular when it became what some people have compared to a cult. And so these new revelations are disturbing and and add a whole other dimension to what we to what we've known about Cesar Chavez and to what in some sense has been an ongoing reassessment of his legacy over the last 20 years. I mean, for people who are not that familiar with his legacy, it's hard to overstate the impact he has had on the labor movement in this country. Um what is your sense about what these allegations do to that movement? I mean, are you concerned that that this could diminish what he did and what others have been building on in the decades since? So, I would say that, you know, his importance as a historic figure is not so much as a labor leader, but in some ways as a civil rights leader, what he was able to do in terms of organizing the first union for farmworkers, who were predominantly Latino at the time, Mexican-American and Mexicans, as well as Filipinos. That accomplishment, that success that he had in convincing poor people and in in in teaching people that they had the ability through organizing to overcome the agricultural industry in in all of its power in California, that is part of the most significant part of his legacy. That has not been the case right now for for many, many years, and one of the things that I write about and others have is the ways in which he in some ways destroyed his own movement or the power of it in terms of its ability to help farmworkers. title: Gen AI in Libraries Conference Poster on AI Tools for Literature Reviews: A Rubric for Evaluation
transcription: Our poster presentation documents the creation of a rubric by a group of librarians at American University to evaluate which AI tools, if any, made sense for us to subscribe to and promote. We ended up creating this rubric ourselves because we couldn't find an already extant tool that fit our needs, and we thought detailing our process might be helpful to other institutions currently considering the adoption of AI tools. Our university librarian asked our department to pilot an AI research tool. This group then decided to review AI tools focused on the literature review process. Literature review tools were selected for a few reasons. One, they're discipline agnostic. We're a social science heavy institution, which tends to be pretty interdisciplinary. Two, faculty, students, and staff all do literature reviews. And three, there are a number of AI tools with literature reviews built specifically in mind. In order to determine how we would evaluate these tools, we met as a group and discussed what we would want a rubric to measure. We reviewed some of the literature related to this, there wasn't much, and determined the questions by consensus. We then created a survey in Qualtrics. We divided up the list evenly between group members, with some claiming tools in which they were particularly interested or had experience with. Then, each member analyzed three to four tools and recorded the results in Qualtrics. Ithaka, the nonprofit behind JSTOR, has created the Ithaka Generative AI Product Tracker that lists generative AI tools that can be used for postsecondary teaching, learning, or research activities. The tracker includes roughly 150 AI tools and counting, many of which support key stages of the research lifecycle, including discovery, understanding, and creation. We went through the entire list and identified 18 AI tools that could help in the literature review process in subject areas within the curriculum at AU. We then developed a shared evaluation framework based on eight criteria. They include, one, access model, whether the tool is free or subscription-based...

title: Gen AI in Libraries Conference Poster on AI Tools for Literature Reviews: A Rubric for Evaluation
transcription: to audience, whether it is useful for students, faculty, or researchers. Three, data sources, including the types of content indexed, disciplinary coverage, international and non-English resources, and access to library subscription content. Four, functionality, including the underlying large language models and customization options. Five, quality, such as citation accuracy, summary accuracy, and relevance of results. Six, privacy, focusing on data collection, data use, and transparency. Seven, impact, whether the tool would improve accessibility of research and library perception of quality, and eight, usability, including user experience and ADA compliance. Bias and misrepresentation are often a result of the corpus and of the algorithms and machine learning used by large language models that power each tool. Matthew Reidsma's 2016 article on library discovery layers tested embedded search tools. Using Reidsma's examples, we tested the AI tools for biases. Five of the AI tools provided misinformation in summaries. In our experience, this is often because the tool is searching in titles and abstracts instead of in the full text. Two of the tools may have shared biased or toxic information. We have also investigated disciplinary variation. One tool did well with non-English language materials but failed to provide satisfactory content for the other disciplines. At least five of the AI tools failed to provide information for one or more disciplines. After our analysis, we contacted vendors and investigated five tools that had potential for literature reviews. We've included a high-level summary of the five tools that we investigated here. Many AI tools are not fully developed and need to be tested with scholars and further customized for literature reviews. We advocate for an investigation of the data sources used by any tool, independent testing of tools to ensure alignment with library values, and a user-centered approach that focuses on support for learning.

title: ICML 2026 | AI Governance Needs ISO-like Interoperability Protocols | Spotlight Presentation
transcription: Good morning, everyone. My name is Rafia Islam, and I'm here to present our position paper, AI Governance Needs ISO-like Interoperability Protocols, Not Just Laws. Our main claim is simple: laws alone cannot make AI governance work across borders. We need shared technical standards to go with them. Let me walk you through why. Here is the problem we start from: AI rules are splitting apart across countries. The European Union has a binding law, the EU AI Act. It sorts systems into four risk levels and requires formal checks before and after release. China takes a registration and security route. Companies must file their algorithms and pass security review for public-facing systems. The United States has no single federal law. It uses sector rules and voluntary guidance, mainly the NIST AI Risk Management Framework. ASEAN offers regional principles, but these are not enforceable. So, we have four regions, four very different philosophies. The strange part is that the underlying systems, the data, and the risks are often the same; only the rules differ. This creates what we call a standardization vacuum. Picture one foundation model with the same weights and the same behavior. Send it to two countries. In one, it is labeled high-risk. In the other, low-risk. Nothing about the model changed, only the border changed. Why does this happen? Because there is no shared technical language for describing AI risk. Without the language, every country classifies the same system in its own way. The result is compliance uncertainty, repeated assessments, and blocked cross-border deployment. And this acts like a hidden trade barrier. Large companies can absorb the cost of dealing with many rule books. Small and medium firms cannot. So, fragmentation quietly favors the big players.

title: ICML 2026 | AI Governance Needs ISO-like Interoperability Protocols | Spotlight Presentation
transcription: So, here is our position. We are not against laws. Laws are necessary. They set the thresholds. They decide what counts as acceptable AI behavior and they carry the enforcement power. But laws are not enough on their own. They cannot guarantee that thousands of different systems in different countries are all measured the same way. That gap needs a second layer. We call it a complementary technical layer. It is a shared, machine-readable way to describe AI risk. In short, laws define what is acceptable, and standards show how you prove it in practice. The two work together. One without the other leaves the job half done. We are not guessing that this works. We have a precedent: GDPR, the European privacy law. GDPR succeeded worldwide, but not because of legal text alone. It succeeded because standards made it actionable. Companies use ISO 27001, a security management standard, to turn legal duties into concrete controls. They also used privacy by design, which builds privacy into systems from the start. Together, the law plus the standards turned an abstract mandate into daily practice. One honest heads up here: ISO 27001 governs how an organization runs its operations. AI is harder because AI governs model outputs, and those outputs are unpredictable and can change over time. So, GDPR guides us, but AI needs standards that can handle that extra uncertainty. This brings us to our proposal: machine-readable AI risk manifests. Think of it as a nutrition label for an AI system. It is a modular JSON file, similar to a software bill of materials. A computer can read it, check it, and compare it automatically. It is not just a document for humans to skim. It travels with the model as a compliance credential. So, one manifest can move across borders. It can plug into MLOps pipelines, into procurement systems, and into regulatory review. As you can see on the right, it is structured data: fields like system identity, intended use, and a risk class that is tagged per jurisdiction. Build it once, reuse it everywhere. We are not asking for hundreds of fields on day one. We propose a minimum baseline of three dimensions, all reported in one shared vocabulary.

title: ICML 2026 | AI Governance Needs ISO-like Interoperability Protocols | Spotlight Presentation
transcription: First, fairness. Report at least one global fairness metric, name the demographic groups, and state your mitigation. Second, sustainability. Report training and inference energy, and disclose the hardware context because energy numbers mean nothing without it. Third, lineage. Give a verifiable record of data sources and hash the data source artifacts so they can be audited later. One important point, these three do not force every country to agree on legal thresholds. They simply let each country read its own rules through one common layer, same data, one format, many interpretations. Now let me address two fair objections. First objection, standards will slow down fast moving research and hurt innovation. Our reply, this assumes that having no standards keeps you nimble. It ignores the coordination cost that fragmentation already imposes at scale. Teams already redo the same work for every jurisdiction. Second objection, compliance requirements favor large established companies and hurt small firms. Our reply, uncoordinated fragmentation already costs small actors more because they must navigate many incompatible regimes. So the real question is not whether standards exist. It is how they are designed. Our answer is to make them modular, versioned, and outcome-oriented. They specify what you must demonstrate and how you must be lit. That is infrastructure, not gatekeeping. So what do we recommend concretely? Three things. One, build open, modular, extensible protocols with low cost paths, reference implementations, and capacity building for the global south and for smaller firms. Two, put stewardship in a multi-stakeholder body such as ISO, IEC, or IEEE releasing major versions on multi-year cycles with room for local modules. Three, treat standards as coordination infrastructure. Embed them in certification, in sandboxes, or and in procurement. They complement the law. They never replace it. The goal is a shift from siloed compliance to interoperable conformance. Comply once, reuse everywhere. That is our position. AI governance needs ISO-like interoperability protocols, not just laws. Thank you for listening. I'm happy to take your questions.

title: MLOX presentation @ CAIN 2026
transcription: Hi everyone, I'm Nico Köhnitz and I'd like to introduce MLOx, open-source MLOps for the rest of us. MLOx is a control plane for self-hosted AI infrastructure. Today, even large organizations struggle with MLOps, and for individuals or small teams, the gap is even bigger. You rely on managed cloud platforms, which are powerful but complex, expensive, and often lead to vendor lock-in. Or you try to build your own stack, which requires significant DevOps expertise and a lot of glue code. In practice, many teams face the same constraints. They don't have the time to operate complex cloud setups. They don't want to commit to a single hyperscaler or multiple ones, and they lack the resources to build and maintain a full system from scratch. MLOx is designed exactly for this setting. The core idea is simple: make it possible to run a complete, secure, and observable ML system on your own infrastructure without needing a dedicated DevOps team. So, the problem is when building machine learning systems, you typically deal with three layers. First: infrastructure - servers, runtimes, security. Second: services - databases, pipelines, tracking, registries, serving. And third: integration - configs, secrets, dependencies, and monitoring. Each of these layers is already complex on its own, and while there are many tools available, most of them focus on just one piece of the puzzle. So what happens in practice is that teams end up stitching together everything themselves, often with fragile scripts and ad-hoc setups. And that leads to a key observation: most tools solve one piece, but the user actually needs the whole system. So what MLOx does, MLOx addresses this by structuring the problem into three parts. First: servers - you define and manage infrastructure, choose a backend like Docker, Kubernetes, or native execution, and monitor it. Second: services - you install and manage components like MLflow, Airflow, or MLServer, including configuration and secrets. And third: wiring.

title: MLOX presentation @ CAIN 2026
transcription: This is where MLOxs becomes interesting. It understands services and how they connect, resolves dependencies, and links everything together. So, instead of manually integrating components, you work off at the level of systems, not individual tools. Right now, lifecycle management is intentionally simple, mostly add and remove, because the focus is on reducing complexity, not adding more layers. The architecture follows a simple but important idea. Users can interact with MLOxs through the CLI, UI, or TUI. So, in practice, they don't need to write configuration files themselves. Under the hood, these interactions are translated into a structured configuration, including servers, services, and their relationships. So, a session loads this configuration together with state and secrets, and builds an internal infrastructure graph. This graph represents how all components are connected. From there, different backends, such as Docker, Kubernetes, or native execution, translate this into actual deployment actions. So, MLOxs acts as a kind of a middle layer, not adding complexity, but absorbing it and exposing a simpler interface. Another important aspect is extensibility. Through a system, a plug-in system, new services, integrations, or even backends can be added without changing the core system. So, MLOxs currently supports multiple backends. Docker is the most complete and stable today. Most services run on Docker. Kubernetes is already supported and being extended with more services. There's also a native mode for lightweight setups and a connector backend for hybrid or external integrations. On top of that, the system is structured in layers: infrastructure, services, integrations, and plug-ins. This makes it possible to grow the ecosystem over time without turning the core idea into a monolith. So, the goal is not to build everything into MLOxs, but to provide a structured way to integrate everything else. Let me give you a very simple example. From the CLI, you can list all registered models with MLOxs model list.

title: MLOX presentation @ CAIN 2026
transcription: Then you can deploy a specific model version to a target server with a single command: mlox model deploy, then the version and the registry and the model, and the target server. What happens under the hood is more interesting. MLOx automatically connects the model registry, retrieves artifacts, configures the serving layer, for example, via MLServer, and ensures everything is deployed securely. So instead of manually wiring together multiple components, you define what you want, and MLOx handles how it connects. So why is this useful? Well, from early usage and feedback, a few patterns emerged. First, integration is the real bottleneck, not individual tools. Second, simplicity wins, especially for small teams. Third, transparency matters. People want to understand what is happening. And fourth, self-hosting becomes viable once complexity is reduced. So in terms of positioning, MLOx sits somewhere between fragile custom custom-built pipelines and large cloud-native MLOps platforms. It tries to combine the flexibility of the first with some of the structure of the second. So looking ahead, there are a few main directions. First, security: better networking, firewall integration, and more advanced certificate handling. Second, features and platform: especially deeper Kubernetes support and improved service integrations. And third, simplicity: lighter alternatives to existing tools, smaller default setups, and potentially separating monitoring into its own application. The guiding principle here is important: not just more features, but more secure and more minimal. So as a takeaway, to summarize, MLOx abstracts servers, services, and their wiring into a single consistent system. It is open-source, self-hosted, and extensible, and designed for teams that need complete systems, not isolated tools. And since this is an early-stage project, we are actively looking for contributors, collaborators, and feedback, and also open to partnerships and funding discussions. If this resonates with you, I'd be very happy to connect. Thank you.

title: CVPR 2026 : CrowdGen
transcription: Let's talk about this paper titled Generative Adversarial Perturbation with Cross-Paradigm Transferability on Localized Crowd Counting. We have seen evasion attacks on all kinds of vision tasks, classification, face recognition to name a few, but crowd models are relatively less explored. They are more complex than the classification task, but they inherit the same weakness that other deep vision models suffer. And most importantly, they are widely deployed in real life scenarios such as public safety, retail analytics and so on. So an undercounting attack could be a safety risk. As we can see a clean example on the right, while passed by a model it outputs 428 people and their locations. However, if small adversarial perturbation is added, it slashes this prediction by over 40% and we get 285 people. So, the previous studies on crowd models are mostly patch-based attacks and they are limited to only density map-based models. So naturally, the question emerges is that can adversarial perturbations transfer across heterogeneous localized crowd counting paradigms such as density map and point regression models? So, to accomplish this attack, we design a perturbation generator that takes clean image as input and outputs the perturbation noise, and this noise is added to the clean image to produce the adversarial image. For black-box transferability, we design a loss function keeping the transferability, imperceptibility and effectiveness goal in mind. Our hypothesis is that even though these models vary by outputs, they share similar backbone architecture such as VGG, ResNet and same weights. So, we our, we hypothesis that this drives the transferability. On the other hand, the crowd scenes are low-frequency dominated, so we suppress the high-frequency and magnitude of the noise for, for subtle perturbation. And lastly, the effectiveness between two paradigms of models come from model-specific loss. So, density map models do the density suppression, and point regression-based models perform logit suppression. Together, this combined loss govern the training. So, this is a sample instance of adversarial examples, where adversarial perturbations are added to the clean images for various lighting conditions.

title: VeriSHAP 5min Summary Presentation
transcription: Hi there, I'm David, and in the next few minutes, I present a short summary of our paper VerifySHAP, or VerySHAP for short, on computing provable bounds for the exact Shapley values of neural networks. SHAP is a popular feature importance technique that can help us explain deep neural networks. The goal is, for example, to find out what influence an input feature, such as the arrow in this image, has on the prediction a neural network makes. SHAP provides such importance scores by computing what is called the Shapley value of each input feature. So, for example, for this arrow feature, we look at a combination of the other features, once with the arrow present, here in yellow, and once with the arrow absent, here in pink. We then use a value function V to mask out the missing features and evaluate the network on that new input with the masked-out features. We then subtract the network output we get when the arrow is absent from the output we get when the arrow is present to compute what is called the contribution delta of this arrow feature. However, SHAP does not only look at one such combination of input features, but looks at all of the combinations of the other input features that we can have. This means that computing Shapley values requires enumerating an exponential number of these feature combinations that are also called coalitions. Because this clearly does not scale very well, previous work has investigated different statistical estimators that only sample a certain number of coalitions. While this is a lot more scalable, these techniques don't necessarily tell us how far off they are with an individual estimate, which can be problematic in sensitive applications. Additionally, for empirically evaluating these SHAP estimators, we need to know the ground-truth exact Shapley values. For these reasons, we introduce VerySHAP, a new algorithm for computing the exact Shapley values of neural networks faster on higher-dimensional feature spaces, and computing guaranteed lower and upper bounds on Shapley values using ideas from neural network verification. The key idea from neural network verification that we leverage is bound propagation. Bound propagation allows us to propagate an entire set of input features, such as this entire coalition space, through the contribution function. And then we obtain a guaranteed lower bound and a guaranteed upper bound on the contribution. We can then plug these bounds into the SHAP equation, and obtain a guaranteed lower bound and a guaranteed upper bound on the Shapley value itself.

title: VeriSHAP 5min Summary Presentation
transcription: While this bound can be rather loose, the way we did it here, since we bound over the entire coalition space, we can iteratively refine the coalition space using a branch and bound approach to create more and more granular partitions of the coalition space. We can again apply bound propagation for each of these partitions to compute guaranteed Shap bounds, and the finer we make that partition, the tighter these bounds get. As we show theoretically, these bounds are indeed guaranteed to contain the true Shapley value at every iteration. We also show that this algorithm eventually recovers the exact Shapley value after finitely many iterations. Another important insight is that, for a linear model, you don't have to do any splitting to compute the exact values. This also has implications for neural networks, as it means that VeriShap can also terminate early for piecewise linear networks, such as ReLU networks, with the exact Shapley value. This also happens in practice, as demonstrated by this MNIST example. Here we compute the exact Shapley value of a ReLU network in 512 iterations, which is way fewer than would be required for enumerating all coalitions. This example also shows that the Shap bounds are useful in their own right. So, for example, the Shapley bounds in iteration 278 already provide us with essentially the same information as the exact values, while taking less time to compute. We compare VeriShap to the previous state-of-the-art algorithm for computing exact Shapley values that is called ExactShap. As this table shows, VeriShap is able to compute exact Shapley values for substantially larger search spaces of up to 2 to the power of 25 coalitions. For computing tight Shap bounds, VeriShap even scales to 60 input features in some cases. We also compared VeriShap to statistical Shap estimators, showing that VeriShap can be advantageous over estimators when high accuracy is required. Additionally, we use VeriShap to compare different Shap estimators on datasets where it was previously infeasible to compute the ground truth Shapley values for neural networks. To summarize, we presented VeriShap, an algorithm for computing guaranteed bounds on Shapley values that, furthermore, eventually recovers the exact Shapley values. We use bound propagation and branch and bound to scale computing exact Shapley values to up to 25 input features and computing tight bounds for even up to 60 input features. Thank you very much for listening. Our paper is on arXiv, the link is in the video description, and if you have questions, please feel free to reach out.

title: Short Introduction of NeighborMAE (CVPR 2026)
transcription: Hello everyone, I'm Liangcong from KU Leuven. I'm glad to present our work, Neighbor MAE: Exploiting Spatial Dependencies between Neighboring Earth Observation Images in Masked Autoencoder Pre-training. The main idea of this work is simple. In Earth observation, images are not isolated samples. They are observations of the continuous Earth's surface. So instead of training masked autoencoder on each image independently, we ask whether neighboring images can provide useful spatial context for masked autoencoder pre-training. Masked image modeling has become a popular self-supervised learning strategy for Earth observation. The model masks parts of an image and learns to reconstruct the missing region. However, most existing MIM methods reconstruct a single image tile independently. This is a simplification of Earth observation data because satellite and aerial images are naturally spatially connected. Neighboring images often share useful information, such as terrain structure, land use, continuity, roads, buildings, and infrastructure patterns. At the same time, neighboring views may also differ in acquisition time, viewpoints, or sensor conditions. This means neighboring images provide varied signals, shared spatial context, and natural variations. Therefore, we ask: can neighboring images provide useful context for masked image modeling? To answer this question, we propose Neighbor MAE, which extends MAE from single image reconstruction to joint reconstruction of neighboring Earth observation images. The method has five main components. First, neighbor sampling: we use geospatial metadata to sample neighboring Earth observation images based on the intersection over union of the spatial footprints.

title: Short Introduction of NeighborMAE (CVPR 2026)
transcription: Images with sufficient overlap are treated as neighbors. Second, relative position encoding. We embed the patch position in a shared normalized coordinate system, which allows the Transformer to understand the spatial relationship between patches from different images. Third, joint reconstruction. Instead of encoding one image independently, we concatenate the visible patches from both neighboring images and feed them into the same MAE encoder. Then the decoder reconstructs the masked region of both images jointly. Through self-attention, the model can learn dependencies across neighboring views. Fourth, dynamic masking ratio. If two neighboring images overlap strongly, reconstruction becomes easier because one image may reveal information about the other. To keep the pretext task challenging, we increase the mask ratio when the IoU between the neighboring images is high. Finally, visibility-aware loss weighting. Some masked pixels in one image may already be visible in the neighboring images. This can create a shortcut when the model simply copies the visible contents. To avoid this, we reduce the reconstruction loss weight for pixels that are visible from the neighbors when copying is too easy. Together, this design allows Neighbor MAE to learn from neighboring images effectively and efficiently. We compare Neighbor MAE with original MAE under the same training conditions. The evaluation includes diverse downstream Earth observation tasks, including image classification and semantic segmentation. We evaluate both linear probing and fine-tuning. As shown on the right, Neighbor MAE consistently improve over MAE across all downstream benchmarks.

title: Short Introduction of NeighborMAE (CVPR 2026)
transcription: This results suggests that neighboring images provide useful contextual information and that NeighborMAE learns more transferable representation than standard MAE. Next, we analyze where the improvements come from. A key question is whether NeighborMAE works simply because it sees more pixels or because neighboring images provide more useful spatial context. To answer this, we compare different ways to extend the input view using the same extra token budget, approximately two times the base input used by standard MAE. The result shows that simply using a larger tile gives only limited improvement. In contrast, neighboring images provide stronger gains because they introduce richer spatial variations rather than a fixed larger field of view. The best performance comes from multi-temporal neighbors, which combines spatial variations from neighboring regions and temporal variations from different observation. This supports our main claim. The gain does not come merely from increasing input size. It comes from learning spatial and temporal dependencies between neighboring Earth observation images. In conclusion, this work highlights an overlooked signal in masked image modeling for Earth observation, the spatial dependencies between neighboring images. We propose NeighborMAE, a spatially aware MIM framework that jointly reconstructs neighboring EO images, which learns stronger and more transferable representation. Our experiment shows consistent improvement over MAE across diverse downstream task and the ablation study confirms that neighboring views provide more useful context than simply enlarging the inputs. Thank you for your listening.

transcription: I'm Brandon Anderson. I'm a upper postdoc fellow here at NERSC, also in the SciDAC AI and computing systems group. And today, I'll be presenting a AI foundation model for 3D molecules and materials, also known as EquiM. So, first off, foundation models. This is a very popular term these days. Models like ChatGPT, we're all familiar with. These are some examples of foundation models, right? AI models that are trained on a vast quantity of data and can be applied across a range of tasks once it's trained. And for science, we're interested in these types of models because we'd like to build, for example, universal algorithms for many different types of scientific data we care about. So, in this case, in this work, we're going to focus on chemical systems, so molecules and materials. Um, what would it take to build a foundation for molecules and materials? Um, so the way we look at that is, we want to understand how do we represent the data, molecules and materials. So, in this work, we're going to argue for breaking down the representation of molecules and materials as atomic systems with 3D points in space and types of atoms, for example, element types attached to them. And if we have a if we have a foundation model that's trained on these collections of atoms, that could be applied across a range of tasks. For example, it can be a universal generative and predictive algorithm. It can generate new molecules and materials, it also predict properties of existing molecules and materials. And can share information across those different tasks. You could use this in drug discovery, battery research, and many other areas. Now, how would you actually build this if you had a collection of atoms and a bunch of datasets with those atoms in? There's two main approaches to building foundation models in the AI community these days, many others, but the two main ones are autoregressive models and bidirectional models. So, BERT is an example of a bidirectional model and ChatGPT is an example of an autoregressive model. Autoregressive models, you're just predicting one token after the other. And bidirectional models means you can corrupt some tokens in your, like for example, sentences and ask the model to predict back the missing words in the sentence at any position. So, it doesn't assume any kind of ordering when you're doing this bidirectional modeling. And for scientific applications, we're going to argue that that's really important, that we don't want to assume that there's a specific chemical ordering of atoms in these molecular or material systems. So, we lean towards bidirectional models in this work.

title: Ultrasound-CLIP(CVPR 2026)
transcription: Hello, everyone. I'm Jiayin Jin from Hangzhou City University. Today, I'm excited to present our CVPR 2024 paper, UltrasoundCLIP: Semantic-Aware Contrastive Pre-training for Ultrasound Image-Text Understanding. Ultrasound is one of the most widely used imaging modalities in clinical practice. However, ultrasound vision-language learning remains under-explored because of heterogeneous diagnostic attributes and weak image-text alignment. To address this problem, we propose a semantic-aware ultrasound vision-language framework, together with a large-scale ultrasound image-text dataset. Unlike natural images, ultrasound images are highly challenging for vision-language learning. First, ultrasound diagnosis involves heterogeneous diagnostic attributes. For the same lesion, radiologists may describe multiple diagnostic attributes, such as echogenicity, margins, internal characteristics, and calcification. Second, ultrasound images from different organs often look visually similar, even though they correspond to completely different anatomical structures and diagnostic semantics. Because ultrasound image-text pairs often exhibit weak semantic alignment, directly applying conventional CLIP-style contrastive learning is insufficient for ultrasound understanding. This motivates the need for semantic-aware ultrasound representation learning. To address these challenges, we first construct US365K, the first large-scale dedicated ultrasound image-text dataset. The dataset contains over 364,000 image-text pairs collected from more than 11,000 clinical cases, spanning diverse organs and pathological findings. More importantly, we introduce UDT, which stands for Unified Ultrasound Diagnostic Taxonomy. UDT standardizes both anatomical hierarchy and ultrasound diagnostic attributes, providing structured semantic knowledge for ultrasound understanding. This taxonomy serves as the semantic foundation of our framework.

transcription: Opti-My can be captured, the workflow of Opti-My can be captured in a four step process. So, basically we first start off with sample collection where we isolate live cancer cells from different tumor types such as biopsy resections, ascites or pleural fluids and blood or bone marrow aspirates. So, we then perform an ex vivo sensitivity test on the isolated cancer cells by treating them with 12 drugs in a mix of combinations based on proprietary design. title: [CVPR 2026] MoECLIP: Patch-Specialized Experts for Zero-shot Anomaly Detection
transcription: Zero-shot anomaly detection, which aims to detect anomalies in unseen categories, has recently attracted significant attention. In this work, we propose MOE-CLIP: Patch-Specialized Experts for Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection. To perform zero-shot anomaly detection, existing studies primarily use pre-trained CLIP models and apply adapter fine-tuning methods to adapt them to the anomaly detection task. However, conventional approaches process all patches in a monolithic, patch-agnostic manner, without considering the unique characteristics of each patch, such as background patches or anomalous patches. To address this, we propose MOE-CLIP, a mixture-of-experts-based CLIP adaptation method that dynamically selects the most suitable expert for each patch. However, simply applying a mixture-of-experts framework leads to a functional redundancy problem among experts, where multiple experts learn highly similar representations instead of diverse knowledge. Therefore, we further propose FOFS and ETF loss, which encourage each expert to learn distinct and complementary knowledge. Here is the framework of our proposed MOE-CLIP. First, the mixture of LoRA experts module is inserted into the vision encoder layers, enabling dynamic expert selection and adaptation according to the characteristics of each image patch. The approach for achieving expert specialization, FOFS, is a technique applied at the input stage that enforces role separation among experts through the LoRA A matrices. Specifically, it decomposes the input feature space into multiple orthogonal subspaces, forcing each expert to observe only its own unique information without physical overlap with other experts.

title: [CVPR 2026] MoECLIP: Patch-Specialized Experts for Zero-shot Anomaly Detection
transcription: In addition, we introduce ETF loss, because even if FOFS provides different inputs to each expert, there is still a risk that the experts' final outputs may become similar again during training. Motivated by the phenomenon known as neural collapse, ETF loss regularizes the final output vectors of the experts, so that they become geometrically well separated and uniformly distributed in an equiangular manner. In summary, FOFS is responsible for input level separation, while ETF loss enforces output level separation. Through this synergy, each expert becomes specialized in handling its own distinct image patch regions. Comprehensive experimental results across 14 benchmark datasets, spanning industrial and medical domains, demonstrate that MoE-CLIP outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods. When we analyzed which image patches each expert attends to, we observed that, in this example, expert one mainly focused on anomalous patches, expert two captured the overall object regions, expert three attended to background regions, while expert four did not focus on any particularly meaningful area for this image. These results indicate that different experts learn distinct roles and collaboratively contribute to anomaly detection. Due to its patch specialized expert design, MoE-CLIP delivers more accurate and fine-grained anomaly localization than existing methods. By incorporating FOFS and ETF loss, we observed a significant reduction in similarity among experts, demonstrating that the proposed methods effectively mitigate redundancy between experts. Thanks for watching this video.

I want to open by pointing out that household food insecurity is a specific scientific concept. It sounds like it should be the opposite of food of food security, but it isn't. Household food insecurity is the inadequate or insecure access to food due to financial constraints at the household level. Food security has been used to refer to everything from our ability to produce enough food domestically to feed our population, food supply chain, access to food banks. Food security therefore is a term inclusive of many problems that have to do with food and people sometimes conflate action on anything related to food with solutions to household food insecurity, which is not correct. So some find it helpful to think about food insecurity as part of consumption poverty uh and so is related to challenges attributable to general affordability, cost of living, labor market outcome inequality, housing, like we like we just heard. Statistics Canada measures household food insecurity using a specific questionnaire that's been agreed upon by researchers to accurately measure household material circumstances. title: Dr. Dutton Address to the Senate Standing Committee on Agriculture and Forestry

In Canada, we address many other important problems without in-kind transfers and end up improving household food insecurity. I'll give you an example from my own research. Old age food, uh, old age security is more generous than social assistance. Um, the research shows that when low-income individuals turn 65 and qualify for these public pensions, their likelihood of being food insecure decreases. I want to point out that old age security is not making households incredibly rich. Uh, in closing, I'm a researcher at a faculty of medicine, and I care about the implications of household food insecurity for Canadians. भी बड़ा जरूरी दूसरा सवाल। भगवान राम के बिना रामायण कैसी और राम के लिए रणबीर कपूर का ही सिलेक्शन क्यों? क्या वाकई में मजा आ रहा है रणबीर को ऐस भगवान राम के रोल में देखकर? देखो यह बात किसी से छुपी नहीं है जब से ट्रेलर के क्लिप्स वायरल होना शुरू हुए थे और अब फाइनली ऑफिशियल वीडियो भी आ गया है, हर किसी ने यश को ऐस रावण टोटली एक्सेप्ट कर लिया है। नो इफ, नो बट, किसी दूसरे एक्टर का नाम तक नहीं लिया जा रहा है जो इस फिल्म में रावण बन सकता था या फिर यश से ज्यादा बेटर तरीके से एग्रेशन, गुस्सा, घमंड, इन सारे एक्सप्रेशन को डिस्प्ले कर सकता था। सबसे बेस्ट डिसीजन था ट्रेलर को यश के सीन के साथ शुरू करना। देखते ही अलग एनर्जी सी फील होने लगती है। उनके डायलॉग्स उनके चेहरे को पूरी तरह मैच कर रहे हैं। यश और रावण मेड फॉर ईच अदर हैं। चाहे आप इस बात को कितना भी कंट्रोवर्शियल क्यों ना समझो लेकिन हां, इस ट्रेलर के बाद काफी लोग ऐसे होंगे जो रावण की वजह से रामायण देखने जाएंगे। लेकिन इस तरीके का कॉन्फिडेंस लोगों को रणबीर के ऊपर फील नहीं हो रहा है, फिर चाहे वो 144p वाला वीडियो हो या फिर 4K एचडी का ट्रेलर। दिक्कत वीडियो क्वालिटी की नहीं है, एक्टर से एक्सपेक्टेशंस की है। ऑनेस्टली ट्रेलर में रणबीर के सीन्स ऑन-ऑफ टाइप के हैं। जब वो ब्लाइंड फोल्ड वाला सीक्वेंस आया, इतनी खुशी हुई ना अंदर से। यह है वो इंडियन सिनेमा विजन जिसके आगे अंग्रेज भी अपनी नजरें नीची कर लेंगे। लेकिन जैसे ही ट्रेलर में आंखों से वो पट्टी हटी, रणबीर पे भरोसा थोड़ा डगमगा सा जाता है। वो भगवान से धीरे-धीरे इंसान जैसे लगना शुरू हो जाते हैं। नोटिस किया, ट्रेलर में जो पास वाले शॉट्स हैं, वो काफी डाले गए हैं जिनका परपज था गॉड वाइब्स लेकर आना, पब्लिक का सर रिस्पेक्ट में झुकाना। बट ईमानदारी से बोलूंगी एक बात, मैंने सोशल मीडिया पे कुछ फैन मेड पोस्टर्स, एआई जनरेटेड इमेजेस देखी हैं जो रणबीर को भगवान राम के रूप में कई ज्यादा डिवाइन तरीके से प्रेजेंट करती हैं। मैं क्या बोलना चाह रही हूं वो शायद आप सौरभ राज जैन को स्क्रीन पे देखकर जो महसूस करते हो, उसे रामायण में रणबीर से कंपेयर करके अच्छे से समझ जाओगे। देखो जैसे शूर्पणखा का रोल है, उसमें रकुल प्रीत का अचानक आना आपकी एक्सपेक्टेशंस को क्रॉस कर जाता है। प्रेजेंटेशन जितना सोचा था उससे भी ज्यादा बेटर निकला। यही सेम बात अरुण गोविल के लिए भी कही जा सकती है। बट वो सेम फार्मूला रणबीर के केस में उतना फिट नहीं बैठ रहा है, उसका उल्टा हो रहा है फिलहाल। याद रखना इस शब्द पे खास जोर दिया है मैंने, फिलहाल। क्योंकि ऐसा भी नहीं है कि ट्रेलर देखकर आप रणबीर से अंधा हेट करने लग जाओ, सीधा उनकी कास्टिंग पे सवाल खड़े करने लग जाओ, या फिर इतना अंधा भी नहीं होना है कि एक्सपेक्टेशंस को मार ही डालो, जो है, जैसा है उसपे सवाल भी ना पूछा जाए। यह दोनों ही कैटेगरी के काम जो कर रहे हैं या तो उनकी आत्मा बिक गई है या फिर बैंक बैलेंस। फैन वॉर्स होते रहेंगे, पेड पीआर भी चलता रहेगा। वैसे भी उन लोगों से क्या एक्सपेक्ट कर सकते हो आप जो भगवान इंद्र के ऐरावत के बारे में कुछ नहीं जानते हैं और भगवान हनुमान को मंकी गॉड कहकर बुलाते हैं। लेकिन इस सब के बीच में रणबीर के पास तगड़ा मौका है टैलेंट के दम पर हेटर्स को अपना फैन बनाने का जिसमें नितेश तिवारी की बहुत ज्यादा हेल्प चाहिए होगी। यह भगवान परशुराम वाला सीन तो बोनस की तरह आ गया ना। कितने लोगों ने पहले

title: Ramayana Trailer REVIEW | Deeksha Sharma
transcription: बचाना था, सच्ची बताना। पता नहीं क्यों हर बार जब रामायण का कंटेंट आने वाला होता है, लोग आदिपुरुष का ज़िक्र करने लग जाते हैं। बट इस बार ट्रेलर में विजुअल्स की क्वालिटी देखने के बाद आपको बड़े हॉलीवुड प्रोजेक्ट से कंपैरिजन शुरू कर देना चाहिए। जिस तरह क्रिस्टोफर नोलन की फिल्म का टिकट खरीद के आप थिएटर नहीं सीधा दूसरी दुनिया में पहुँच जाते हो, ठीक वैसे ही रामायण ने खुद का हिस्टोरिकल वर्ल्ड क्रिएट किया है। लेकिन सच ये है कि ट्रेलर में जो मॉन्स्टर्स क्रिएट किए गए हैं, वो टीज़र से तो बेहतर हैं लेकिन एकदम बेस्ट रिजल्ट से काफी दूर हैं, वर्क इन प्रोग्रेस लग रहा है, टीवी सीरियल जैसा वाइब आ सकता है कुछ लोगों को। और जिस तरह ट्रेलर का कलर फिक्स किया है, उसी तरह बाकी छोटी-मोटी चीज़ों को रिलीज आने तक संभाल लिया जाएगा। लेकिन मुझे बिल्कुल समझ नहीं आ रहा है, कुछ लोगों का साई पल्लवी को जबरदस्ती डाउनग्रेड करना। माता सीता की पहचान ही यही है कि उनसे जुड़ी सिंपल चीजें भी बहुत बड़ी बन जाती हैं। कितने अच्छे से ड्रेस सिलेक्शन किया है ट्रेलर में साई पल्लवी के सारे सीन्स का। उनके एक्सप्रेशंस देखकर एक प्योर डिवाइन एनर्जी सी आ गई है आँखों में। डायलॉग्स भी बहुत रियल, नेचुरल और इमोशनल फील दे रहे हैं। साई पल्लवी, रणबीर के सीन्स बिल्कुल वैसे हैं, जैसा आप इस एनिमेटेड फिल्म को देखकर फील करना चाहते थे। वैसे अब रियलाइज हुआ मुझे, क्यों वो दिल्ली वाले इवेंट के बाद हर कोई ट्रेलर के म्यूजिक के बारे में बात करते नहीं थक रहा था। लास्ट में देखा, कैसे शोर, सन्नाटा साथ में फील हो रहा था। कहीं से तो न्यूज़ उड़ी है, टी-सीरीज़ ने रामायण के दोनों पार्ट्स के म्यूजिक राइट्स 75 करोड़ में खरीदे हैं और ऑनेस्टली ट्रेलर का बीजीएम सुनके ये प्राइस मुझे तो डिस्काउंट जैसा लग रहा है। देखो एज टोटल, इस ट्रेलर ने रामायण की हिस्ट्री को अच्छे से इकट्ठा कर लिया है। बहुत तगड़ी डिटेलिंग कर रहे हैं नितेश तिवारी जो छोटी-छोटी चीजों में साफ़ नजर आ रहा है। ट्रोल करने वाले चाहे कुछ भी बोले, बट रामायण की फिल्म मेकिंग अपने सब्जेक्ट को डिसरिस्पेक्ट बिल्कुल नहीं कर रही है, उल्टा एक फैमिलियर सब्जेक्ट को भी नया सा फील दे दिया है, एक्साइटमेंट आने लगा है। काफी लोग सवाल कर रहे थे ना कि रामायण का हाइप सिर्फ इसीलिए है क्योंकि वो रामायण है, उसका सब्जेक्ट हर किसी के साथ कनेक्ट करता है, इसके अलावा फिल्म की टीम ने अलग से इसमें क्या ऐड किया है? कास्टिंग 100 में 100 नंबर, ऑडियो सुनके सुकून आता है, एक्शन बहुत बड़े स्केल का होगा और इमोशंस सच्ची में भगवान के करीब ले जाते हैं। और कुछ चाहिए? सुबह 4:00 बजे उठकर नई जनरेशन के बच्चे इंडियन फिल्म के ट्रेलर का वेट कर रहे हैं, कुछ तो अच्छा किया होगा ना? जब गालियां देने में इतना आगे रहते हो तो क्रेडिट देने में कंजूसी क्यों करना? लेकिन इस बात से भी इनकार नहीं कर सकते कि फाइनल क्वालिटी में अभी काफी काम करना पड़ेगा क्योंकि क्रिएचर्स वगैरह थोड़े आर्टिफिशियल लग रहे हैं, उनमें रियलिटी वाली बात नहीं है। लेकिन एक चीज़ मेरे दिमाग में जरूर आ रही है, जो बिना बोले मैं रह नहीं पाऊँगी। अगर रामायण पार्ट वन भगवान राम के बारे में ज्यादा है और इसमें रावण का स्क्रीन टाइम काफी कम होगा, उसके बावजूद यश ने अगर इस तरह पकड़ बना ली है फिल्म पे तो फिर सोचो फिल्म के पार्ट टू में क्या होगा? जब रामायण का फोकस यश पे शिफ्ट करेगा, रावण तो हार जाएगा लेकिन क्या यश को रणबीर हरा पाएंगे? कोई भी यार नहीं, कोई ट्रोल नहीं, अगर आप एक जिंदा सिनेमा लवर हो तो फ्रैंकली दो बातें जरूर लिखकर बताओ, जो आपको ये ट्रेलर देखकर सबसे पहले दिमाग में आईं। टीज़र के बाद ट्रेलर में क्या सुधर गया और आगे क्या सुधारा जा सकता है? दिल खोलके कमेंट करके जरूर बताना। मेरी मानो तो इंडियन सिनेमा का नया जन्म हो चुका है दोस्त। बोलो जय श्री राम। टेक केयर, बाय-बाय।

title: Ramayana Trailer Review | Yogi Bolta Hai
transcription: तो फाइनली वो दिन आ गया जिसका सब लोग वेट कर रहे थे। रामायण का, नाना, नमित मल्होत्राज़ रामायण का एक प्रॉपर ट्रेलर इज़ आउट नाउ ऑन सोशल मीडिया। वो भी ढेर सारे लीक्स के बाद। यार, आप ट्रेलर लॉन्च इवेंट एंड ट्रेलर को सोशल मीडिया पे अपलोड एक साथ करोगे तो ये लीक्स करना फिर उस लीक्स को हटाने के लिए एक एजेंसी को हायर करना ये सब नहीं होता। बट एनीवेज़, पैसा है तो करो ख़र्चा। राजामौली ने मस्त काम किया था भाई। इवेंट रखा और जिस टाइम पे इवेंट में ट्रेलर दिखाया था वाराणसी का, उसी टाइम पे सोशल मीडिया पे डाल दिया था। एनीवेज़, ट्रेलर आया है तो भाई बात करना तो बनता है। वेल, हेलो, मेरा नाम है योगी और हमारी मुलाकात बार-बार होगी। सबसे पहले अब मैं यहाँ खुल के कह सकता हूँ कि रावण का जो लुक अभी आपने ट्रेलर में देखा या लॉर्ड परशुराम का जो ग्लिम्प्स आपने अभी ट्रेलर में देखा या इवन कुंभकरण, वो हमने क्रिएटर इवेंट में मुंबई में देखा था नमित मल्होत्रा जी के घर। आई मीन इसके अलावा भी बहुत कुछ देखा था, ऐरावत वाली लड़ाई और कुछ एक कैरेक्टर्स। तो वही कुछ एक सेम कैरेक्टर्स इसमें भी दिखाए गए हैं एंड आई मस्ट से कि इस 4 मिनट के ट्रेलर में रावण के कैरेक्टर में यश बस कमाल ही करते नज़र आ रहे हैं। सी, आई एम नॉट ग्लोरिफाइंग रावण, बट आई एम टॉकिंग अबाउट यश की परफॉर्मेंस। एंड पूरा ट्रेलर देखने के बाद आई कैन प्राउडली से कि जितनी भी कास्टिंग की गई है वो एकदम ऑन पॉइंट लग रही है। अब देखो कोई बोलेगा कि रावण का कैरेक्टर इतना मस्त एक्शन वगैरह करते हुए दिखाया है, अग्रेशन में दिखाया है और रणबीर एज़ श्री राम को एकदम ठंडा सा दिखा दिया। भाई, वी आर नाउ हैबिचुअल टू सी मेनस्ट्रीम एक्टर्स इन टॉक्सिक मेल पर्सनालिटी। कबीर सिंह में शाहिद का अग्रेशन देख लो आप, रणबीर कपूर को एनिमल में पसंद किया गया था क्योंकि वो अग्रेशन से भरा हुआ था, यश को केजीएफ में पसंद किया गया था क्योंकि अगेन अल्फा मेल मस्क्युलिनिटी, मार्को में उन्नी मुकुंदन को, द बॉयज़ में होमलैंडर को, सेम विद पुष्पा, सेम विद अदर ग्रे शेड्स एंड एंटी-हीरो टाइप कैरेक्टर्स क्योंकि वो अग्रेशन एंड मार-धाड़ एंड टॉक्सिसिटी से भरे हुए थे एंड आजकल लोगों को वही पसंद भी आता है भाई। यहाँ रणबीर राम हैं भाई, वो जैसे थे वैसा ही प्रेजेंट किया गया है शांत मर्यादा वाले। एंड आई डोंट हैव एनी डाउट कि रणबीर एज़ श्री राम वैसा ही अपना कैरेक्टर को प्ले करेंगे जैसी रिक्वायरमेंट श्री राम की परफॉर्मेंस के लिए सूट करेगी। यश तो एब्सोल्यूट जेम लग ही रहे हैं। ही इज़ लाइक जैसे रामानंद सागर के रावण के बाद अगर कोई रावण सूट हुआ है तो वो यश ही हैं। इवन ईच एंड एवरी कैरेक्टर इज़ सूटेड फॉर देयर रोल। तो मैं कास्टिंग एंड उनके परफॉर्मेंस को लेकर कोई नेगेटिव पॉइंट ज़बरदस्ती नहीं रखना चाहूँगा। लेकिन जहाँ हम सबको पता है अबाउट रामायण, वहाँ हम इस फ़िल्म में बस प्रेजेंटेशन के लिए उत्साहित हैं एंड डैम, द प्रेजेंटेशन! रावण का वो पहला शॉट, वो एक लात से दरवाज़ा, आई मीन उतना बड़ा ह्यूज़ द्वार भव्य

title: Ramayana Trailer Review | Yogi Bolta Hai
transcription: कुबेर द्वार को तोड़ देना फिर कुबेर की नगरी में आने के बाद वो जटाएं यार वो एंड दैट फाइट सीक्वेंस इस ऑन अनदर लेवल भाई। अपेरेंटली रावण अपने भाई कुबेर के राज्य को ही लंका में कन्वर्ट करता है उस पर विजय पाकर तो जहां वो वाइट एंड ब्लूइश एंड गोल्डन बिल्डिंग स्ट्रक्चर आपको दिख रहा है वो लंका ही है। उसके बाद वो महल के बालकनी में आकर सबको अपने किंग होने की घोषणा कर रहा है। दिस इज व्हाट वी कॉल्ड प्रेजेंटेशन। जो बर्फ में या हिमालयन पहाड़ियों में जो लड़ाई दिखाई गई है वो इंद्र के राज्य को लेकर उनसे सिंहासन छीनने वाली लड़ाई होगी। जहां इंद्र को तो नहीं दिखाया गया लेकिन वो ऐरावत वाला सीन भी बहुत ब्यूटीफुली डिजाइन किया गया है। वन मोर थिंग आई नोटिस कि इन्होंने जो राक्षस क्रिएचर्स हैं उनका कलर थोड़ा ह्यूमन्ली रखा है। पिछले टीज़र में जैसा था वैसा नहीं है एंड इवन ट्रेलर के क्रिएचर्स में देखोगे तो वो माथे पे वाइट एंड लाल टीका वगैरा दिया गया है तो चेंजेस तो किए गए हैं लोगों की बातों को ध्यान में रखते हुए। इवन कुछ एक सीन्स तो आई रियली लव्ड जैसे दैट मिथिला में श्रीराम का धनुष बाण उठाने वाला वो सीन। शूर्पणखा के एंट्री एक रथ पे हो रही है जिसमें वाइट लायन जैसे कुछ क्रिएचर्स है। आई मीन इसमें काफी अच्छे से एक मीनिंगफुल क्रिएटिव लिबर्टी ली गई है। एंड अगेन आई कैन से रकुल प्रीत सिंह एज़ शूर्पणखा डैम्न गुड कास्टिंग। एक और सीन बहुत ही ज्यादा खूबसूरत लगा मुझे, जटायु और रावण का युद्ध भाई ये सीन जिस तरह से ट्रेलर में दिख रहा है ना आई कैन ऑनेस्टली इमेजिन। यस, ऑनेस्टली इमेजिन कि ये सीन इस फिल्म का वन ऑफ द बेस्ट विजुअल सीन होगा। विवेक ओबेरॉय का विद्युतज्वा कैरेक्टर एंड रावण का एक फाइट सीक्वेंस भी हम देखते हैं ट्रेलर में। विद्युतज्वा एक्चुअली शूर्पणखा का पति होता है। और भी कई सारे कैरेक्टर्स हैं इसमें जो रिवील होते हैं एंड कास्टिंग किस-किस की है उसके ऊपर मैं ऑलरेडी एक डिटेल वीडियो बना चुका हूं तो वो चेक आउट जरूर कर लेना। इस ट्रेलर में कैकसी यानी रावण की मदर, रावण का भाई कुंभकरण को भी दिखाया गया है। मंथरा है, राजा दशरथ है, मारीच है। इवन भाई, लास्ट सीन में रावण का हायना जैसा दिखने वाला पालतू जानवर भी दिखाया गया है जिसका नाम क्रोधा रहता है जिसको इनके कॉमिक बुक्स में भी दिखाया गया है एंड दैट सीन एंड दैट रेज एक्सप्रेशन बाय यश इज एब्सोल्युटली कमेंडेबल। वैसे इतना सब दिखाने के बाद भी एग्जैक्ट रिलीज डेट अभी भी रिवील नहीं की गई है यानी दिवाली में तो आएगी पिक्चर लेकिन कौन से दिन वो नहीं पता फिलहाल। तो भाई, डेट जो भी हो, द वर्ल्ड इज नॉट रेडी फॉर दिस। अच्छा मेकर्स, अगर आप ये मेरा वीडियो देख रहे हैं तो वो जो एक शॉट है जहां रावण दौड़ते हुए कुबेर के सैनिकों की ओर भाग रहा है वो विजुअली थोड़ा पता नहीं क्यों बट ऑकवर्ड सा लग रहा है। इफ यू कैन फिक्स इट, प्लीज फिक्स इट। बाकी मेरे सब्सक्राइबर्स और व्यूअर्स से विनती है कि अगर आपकी भी कोई राय है तो कमेंट में जरूर बता देना। मिलते हैं अगले वीडियो में। बाय।

title: PE Fund Journal Entry Bible | Private Equity Accounting Interview Guide
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Most candidates memorize PE journal entries and still fail the interview. Why? Because the interviewer is not testing debit and credit only. They are testing cash, NAV, investor capital and LP reporting. Take one private equity fund case: commitment $100 million, capital called $20 million, investment made $15 million, fund expense $1 million, management fee $2 million, fair value $18 million, exit $18 million, distribution to LPs $5 million. Here is the scoreboard. After every entry, ask: did cash move? Did NAV move? Capital activity or performance? What reaches LP reporting? First, capital call. The fund calls 20 million from LPs. Debit cash 20 million, credit investor capital 20 million. Cash increases, investor capital increases, but performance has not improved. This is capital activity, not income. Capital call brings cash, it does not create profit. Second, investment made. The fund invests 15 million into a portfolio company or SPV. Debit investment 15 million, credit cash 15 million. Cash goes down, investment asset goes up, but there is no immediate gain. Cash became investment, that is the trap. Investment made is not an expense and it does not automatically increase NAV. Third, fund expense. Assume 1 million of audit, legal or admin expense. Debit fund expense 1 million, credit expense payable or cash 1 million. This hits P&L, so NAV reduces. LP reporting shows fund level expense impact. The trap: fund expense is not capital activity. It reduces NAV because it hits P&L.

title: PE Fund Journal Entry Bible | Private Equity Accounting Interview Guide
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Credit cash 5 million. Cash leaves the fund. Investor capital reduces, but distribution does not automatically mean profit. It may be return of capital, realized gain, income, recallable distribution or a mix. That affects DPI, LP statements, capital accounts and callable capital. The trap: distribution is the cash event. Classification tells the performance story. Eighth, profit allocation. At period end, fund performance flows into investor capital accounts. Debit P&L or income summary, credit investor capital. This updates the capital account, and the capital account becomes the investor level story. A fund accountant does not stop at P&L. They explain how performance reaches each LP. Now the strategy layer. Different PE strategies add different support schedules. LBO may add SPV books, debt and interest. Fund of funds may add underlying fund investments. Private credit may add interest, PIK, non-accrual or impairment. Real estate may add rent and valuation marks. Distressed may add write downs. But the core logic stays the same. Cash, asset, P&L, NAV, capital account, LP reporting. Before answering any PE journal entry question, ask: Did cash move? Did NAV move? Did P&L move? Capital activity or performance? Realized or unrealized? Accrual or payment? What changed investor capital? What reaches LP reporting? A weak candidate memorizes journal entries. A strong candidate explains the story behind the entries. In private equity fund accounting, the journal entry is not the final answer. The NAV impact, capital account impact and LP reporting impact are the real answer. Follow the Fund Desk for more PE fund accounting interview guides.

title: Journal Your Best Reality ✨ How to Manifest Your Dream Life Through Writing.
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Have you ever felt like you were just one step away from the life you actually want to live, but you just cannot seem to grab it? We have all been there. You have these big dreams and deep desires, but they feel like they are stuck in some alternate reality that you can only see from a distance. Well today, I want to share something with you that completely shifted everything for me. It is not magic and it is not just wishful thinking. It is the intentional practice of journaling to attract your best reality. I used to think journaling was just for recording what happened during my day like a diary, but once I realized it could be a tool for creation, my whole world changed. First, let us talk about why this actually works. When you put pen to paper, you are doing more than just writing words. You are focusing your energy, and giving your subconscious mind a clear roadmap. Most of the time our brains are cluttered with thousands of random thoughts, but journaling forces you to slow down and get specific. It is like sending a clear signal to the universe saying, 'this is exactly what I am ready for.' Your brain has a filtering system called the reticular activating system, and when you write down your desires, you are essentially telling that system what to look for in the real world. The first thing I always do before I start writing is get into a state of gratitude. You cannot manifest from a place of lack because the energy of wanting something often carries the heavy feeling of not having it. So, I start by listing three things I am genuinely thankful for right now. It could be as simple as a good cup of coffee, a supportive friend, or even just the fact that I have a quiet moment to myself. This shifts your vibration from 'I need' to 'I appreciate' which is the perfect foundation for attracting more. Now, let us get into the most powerful part of my routine, which is called scripting. Scripting is basically writing about your future as if it is happening right now, in the present tense. Instead of saying, 'I want to have my dream job,' you would write, 'I am so incredibly happy and fulfilled in my new career.' You have to get detailed. What does your office smell like? How does it feel when you see your name on that door? Who are you celebrating with at dinner tonight? The key is to involve all your senses. When you write these details, your brain starts to believe it is a memory rather than a distant hope. This bridge between your current reality and your desired one is where

title: How Data Centers Actually Work
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Every email you send, every video you stream, and every file stored in the cloud exists somewhere physically. Behind the internet is a network of buildings filled with servers, electrical infrastructure, and cooling systems working continuously to keep data moving. These buildings are called data centers. In this video series, we are going to explain how data centers actually work from a mechanical and electrical perspective, focusing on the systems that keep servers powered, cooled, and operating without interruption. This first video provides the big picture overview. We will explain what a data center does, why these facilities consume so much energy, and why mechanical and electrical systems are the most critical part of the building. In the following videos, we will begin breaking down each system in greater detail. At its simplest level, a data center is a facility designed to store, process, and distribute digital information. Inside the building are rows of servers, which are specialized computers responsible for storing, computing, and network traffic. Unlike office computers that operate intermittently, servers operate continuously. They run 24 hours a day, every day of the year. This creates an important reality. Servers consume large amounts of electricity, and nearly all of that electrical energy eventually becomes heat. While most people think of data centers as IT facilities, from an engineering perspective, they are really energy conversion buildings. Electricity goes in, computing work is performed, and heat comes out. The entire facility exists to manage that process safely and reliably. Every data center, regardless of size, must solve three fundamental problems. The first is continuous power. Servers cannot simply shut down when power is lost. Even brief interruptions can cause data loss or service outages affecting thousands or even millions of users. As a result, power systems must remain available even when equipment fails or utility power is interrupted. The second problem is continuous cooling. Because servers generate heat constantly, cooling systems must also operate continuously. title: How Data Centers Actually Work

transcription: And those concepts will be covered in a later video in this series. Although data centers appear complex, most of the infrastructure falls into three major system groups. The first group is electrical systems. Electrical infrastructure brings power into the building and distributes it safely to server equipment. This includes utility connections, switchgear, backup power systems, and power distribution equipment. The goal is simple. Power must always be available. The second group is mechanical cooling systems. Mechanical systems remove the heat generated by servers. Depending on the facility, this may include chillers, cooling towers, pumps, air handling units, or specialized cooling equipment located directly at the server racks. The objective is to keep equipment operating within safe temperature ranges at all times. The third group is controls and monitoring systems. Controls tie electrical and mechanical systems together into one operating environment. These systems monitor temperatures, power usage, equipment status, and alarms, allowing the facility to automatically respond to changing conditions or equipment failures. In modern data centers, controls and monitoring are just as important as the physical equipment itself. Data centers are often misunderstood because they look similar to commercial buildings from the outside, but operationally, they are very different. In an office building, occupancy changes throughout the day, cooling loads rise and fall, and equipment cycles on and off. In a data center, electrical loads are constant, cooling demand is continuous, and systems rarely shut down. Failure tolerance is also very different. A comfort cooling failure in an office building creates discomfort. A cooling or power failure in a data center can create immediate operational risk. Because of this, data centers typically include redundant equipment, multiple power paths, and system designs that allow maintenance without shutting the facility down. This is hard to identify because you think, "This is just normal tiredness." Be alert of increases in duration and frequency. Any increase is a red flag. Number two, skyrocketing heart rate. My runs pushed me to max zones way too often. What was moderate became intense. Your body is basically screaming, "Slow down." Number three, sleep quality goes down. Exercise should help sleep, right? Nope, mine tanked. And this is essentially because too much exercise stimulates hormones to be elevated at the wrong times, leading to anxiety and body still on edge at night. For example, cortisol levels are elevated throughout the day and night. Number four, moody without workouts. Skip a run, felt off, guilty, irritable. Turns out it's hormone havoc from overdoing it, not just missing the endorphins.

title: Exercise Burnout & Anxiety: My Recovery Story
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: I will deep dive into my sleep routine in a future video, but here's the quick blueprint. Winding mentally down at work around 5:00 to 6:00 p.m. No heavy or triggering workloads. At home, fuel up with a solid evening meal. No skipping. Do meditation or do other mindfulness exercises and boost with supplements like magnesium bisglycinate or phosphatidylserine for that Zen shutdown. Number two, reverse hockey stick. Manage your cortisol levels. Don't eliminate cortisol. Restore its natural rhythm. Upside down hockey stick. Peak high in the morning, then taper gradually to low by bedtime. Maximize the AM surge with hydration, sunlight exposure around 10 to 15 minutes, and light exercise after waking. Also take your coffee in the morning if you are a coffee drinker. During the day, monitor stress and ease off heavy tasks by 4:00 to 5:00 p.m. Try chamomile tea or a short break. At home, fully unplug. No emails or emotional triggers to ensure a smooth wind down. Number three, ego be gone approach. Dial down workout intensity. I quit cold turkey for a month during peak burnout. Nearly fainted on a walk. Post-recovery, easy walks, then moderate runs. Your smartwatch tracks it. Drop to 4 days a week using Phil Maffetone's MAF method. Build sustainable stamina without the crash. Gym? Lighter weights, no heavy squats. But here's the twist. These fixes run deeper than you think with hidden pitfalls and game-changing easy tweaks I discovered the hard way. Want that surge of energy, razor-sharp clarity, and unbreakable strength back? You'll need the full story, including the one mistake that almost derailed my recovery forever. See you in the next video. मुझे क्या दिक्कत है? पता चल जाए मुझे बस। तो हॉस्पिटल पहुँचा। हॉस्पिटल पहुँचा, तो उन्होंने ईसीजी किया और उसके बाद जो है शायद बीपी वगैरह भी चेक किया था उन्होंने। और फिर वो आप डॉक्टर आपस में बात करने लगे। उन्होंने मुझे एक फिर दवाई दी और उनमें से किसी ने आके बोला, उन्होंने मतलब उनके अब बोलने का अंदाज ये था कि कुछ नहीं, पैनिक अटैक है। उस पल एक एक चीज़ समझ में नहीं आती है जब वो डॉक्टर आपको ये कहता है ना कि कि पैनिक अटैक है, तो आपको ऐसा लग रहा होता कि यार ऐसे कैसे हो सकता है? title: How to Stop Panic Attacks: 5 Tools for Anxiety Recovery (My Story as a Single Mum)
